_note: Authored mnemonics and illustration scenes. `rank` is the join key into src/domain/vocabulary/data/vocabulary.json (unique across all 4147 ranked entries; `thai` is NOT unique — 139 spellings repeat). Only `mnemonic` is merged into vocabulary.json and shipped to the browser; everything else is build-time input for scripts/generate-mnemonic-images.py. Style, aspect ratio, quality and negative prompt live in that script, never here.

_tone_glyphs.—: mid — flat, sits in the middle
_tone_glyphs.▁: low — flat, sits at the bottom

entries.mnemonic: A waiter carries one cup of tea across an enormous lawn and sets it down on a single marked flagstone — not that table, this one. thîi pins a thing to its place: at, in, on. (↓ falling, the cup lands and settles)
entries.headline: thîi…
entries.scene: A white-gloved waiter bending to place a single porcelain teacup onto a small round table standing alone in the middle of a vast manicured lawn, a grand palace facade far behind. Long evening shadows stretching across the grass.

entries.mnemonic: A stunt rider is asked whether he can clear the canyon. He gives a thumbs-up — "dâi" — the same sound as DIE, which is exactly what the crowd behind him expects. He can, and he does. Dâi is the can, the got, the managed-it. (↓ falling, the thumb comes down as the engine opens up)
entries.headline: dâi!
entries.scene: A helmeted stunt rider on a motorbike balanced at the lip of a wide desert canyon, giving a confident thumbs-up back over his shoulder to a small crowd of horrified onlookers with their hands on their heads.

entries.mnemonic: A German friend is asked about every plan for the week — the beach, the diving, the noodles — and answers each one with a short flat "Ja." Said the English way, jà. Every ja shoves the action into the future. That is จะ. (▁ low and clipped, each ja a single short beat)
entries.headline: Jà.
entries.scene: A sunburnt traveller counting plans off on his fingers to a grinning backpacker sitting on a guesthouse step, who is nodding firmly with one thumb raised. Dive gear and a packed rucksack lean against the wall beside them. Bright morning light.

entries.mnemonic: A receptionist ends every sentence with a small dip of the head, and every dip carries the same soft sound: "cah", car with the R swallowed. Women hang it on the end of a statement the way the head dips. Leave it off and the sentence lands bare. (↓ falling, the head drops with the voice)
entries.headline: …kâ.
entries.scene: A hotel receptionist in a neat uniform standing behind a marble desk, head bowed and palms pressed together toward a guest she is handing a key to. Her whole posture is a small polite dip.

entries.mnemonic: คะ and ค่ะ are the same soft syllable from the same woman; only the pitch differs. ค่ะ drops, and that is a full stop. คะ stays up high and holds the sentence open, because a question cannot end flat. The pitch is the question mark. (▲ high and taut, the sentence left hanging)
entries.headline: …khá?
entries.scene: A shopkeeper in her doorway leaning slightly towards a customer, one eyebrow lifted, chin raised, palm open in a polite enquiring gesture. Beside her a second woman stands square and settled, hands folded, head level. Warm afternoon light through the open shopfront.

entries.mnemonic: A SWAT team smashes through the door, rifles up — then the lead officer lowers his weapon, presses his palms together and says softly, "sa-WAT-dee." The whole squad copies him. Even a raid starts with hello. (— levels out flat and calm on dee)
entries.headline: Sa-WAT-dee.
entries.scene: Four armoured SWAT officers stand in a smashed doorway, rifles lowered; the leader presses his palms together in a bowing wai greeting. Dusty Thai apartment interior, daylight flooding through the broken door.

entries.mnemonic: A man in a gold suit walks round the room pointing at things and saying the same word each time: "Me. Me. Me." The car indoors, the chandelier, the dog — everything he points at, he has. mii is having, and there being. (— flat and level, the same note every time)
entries.headline: Me. Me. Me.
entries.scene: A man in a loud gold suit standing in a crowded living room jabbing his finger at a sports car parked absurdly indoors, then a chandelier, then a small dog. Every surface is piled with possessions. Bright glittering light.

entries.mnemonic: A raccoon in hotel uniform bows to every guest and addresses each one the same way. Take the end of rac-coon and put breath behind the k: khun. It is the polite you that goes in front of anybody's name. (— flat and level, unfailingly polite)
entries.headline: Khun…
entries.scene: A raccoon standing upright in a braided doorman's uniform and white gloves, bowing deeply with one paw extended towards a startled guest with a suitcase. Brass luggage trolley, revolving door, polished marble lobby, warm chandelier light.

entries.mnemonic: A queue of dancers waits at an audition and the director asks who is next. Every finger in the line swings toward one woman, and she points back at her own chest — "chǎn?" — me. Chǎn is I, the one being pointed at. (↑ rising, the finger and the voice go up together)
entries.headline: Chǎn?
entries.scene: A line of dancers waiting along a bare rehearsal-room wall, all of them pointing sideways at one woman near the middle, who has turned and is pointing back at her own chest with both hands, eyebrows up.

entries.mnemonic: A man introduces himself and lays his open palm flat on his own chest, the voice climbing as it comes — phǒm. The palm on the chest is the word: a man saying I. (↑ rising, the voice lifts as the hand presses in)
entries.headline: Phǒm.
entries.scene: A Thai man in a pressed shirt at a formal introduction, standing straight and pressing his open palm flat against the centre of his own chest, head slightly bowed, smiling. Another man faces him with a hand half extended.

entries.mnemonic: A giant ape sits on a mountain of treasure and pats each piece in turn: the crown, the anchor, the ship's bell. All of it is the treasure of Kong. khɔ̌ɔng hooks a thing to its owner. (↑ rising, the voice climbs as he lifts each piece)
entries.headline: …khɔ̌ɔng Kong.
entries.scene: A colossal ape seated on a heaped mound of gold, crowns and ship's anchors on a rocky island, holding one glittering crown up to the light between two fingers, thoroughly satisfied. Tiny sailors stare up from a boat far below. Dawn sky.

entries.mnemonic: Everyone leaving the beach bar waves at the barmaid on their way out: "bye, Dee." She is comfortable, she is good, and she answers without lifting her head out of the hammock. Sà-baai-dii is sabai plus dii — comfortable-good, the standard answer to how are you. (— the last syllable lands flat and easy, nothing wrong at all)
entries.headline: Bye, Dee!
entries.scene: A barmaid lying back in a hammock strung behind a bamboo beach bar, one hand raised in a lazy wave, eyes closed and smiling. Two customers walk away down the sand waving back over their shoulders.

entries.mnemonic: Two friends on a bench are handed one cup between them and drink it together, heads almost touching, one on each side of it. Coffee with milk, her with him — everything paired goes through kàp. (▁ low and flat, a cup set down on the table)
entries.headline: …kàp…
entries.scene: Two young friends on a low bench at a roadside drinks stall, leaning in from opposite sides to share a single tall iced coffee with two straws, shoulders touching, both laughing. Plastic stools, a steel kettle, dappled light through leaves.

entries.mnemonic: A toddler reaches for the cake and his grandmother's hand comes down flat over it: "mâi!" It is the same MY as the question word ไหม, but slammed down instead of lifted up. Not, no, don't. The tone does all the work. (↓ falling, the hand and the voice drop together)
entries.headline: Mâi!
entries.scene: A kitchen table with a whole iced cake on it. A small boy on tiptoe stretches for the edge of the plate while an old woman's hand lands flat across the top of the cake, her other hand raised.

entries.mnemonic: Two words the learner already has: tham, to do, and ngaan, the job. A clerk presses his inked thumb onto form after form, one for every hour of the shift, and the pile never gets smaller. Doing the job: tham-ngaan, to work. (— both syllables flat, the same stamp over and over)
entries.headline: tham-ngaan.
entries.scene: A tired clerk at a government desk pressing his inked thumb onto a sheet from a tower of identical forms, another tower already done beside him. Ink pad, worn wooden counter, a queue of people blurred behind the glass.

entries.mnemonic: Rain hits at night and the whole street is suddenly indoors — faces at every lit window, nobody left outside. Say night and drop the t: nai. Everything is in. (— flat and level, the rain holding one note)
entries.headline: nai
entries.scene: A narrow Thai street in heavy night rain, empty of people, every shophouse window above glowing warm and crowded with faces looking out. Water sheets off the awnings and runs down the road, reflecting the lights.

entries.mnemonic: A market vendor holds up a mango; the customer points at his own chest — "MY?" — voice climbing at the end the way an English question does. That climb is the question: ไหม turns any sentence into one. (↑ rising, the voice lifts like an eyebrow)
entries.headline: MY?
entries.scene: Bustling Thai street market at golden hour. A smiling vendor in an apron holds a ripe mango out across her fruit stall. Facing her, a young foreign traveller points at his own chest with both index fingers, eyebrows raised high, mouth open in an exaggerated questioning expression.

entries.mnemonic: A traffic cop hands back the wallet you dropped, and the thanks is already built into the word: คุณ khun means you, so khàawp-khun is thanks-you, and the cop is standing right there to collect it. Palms together, head down, the first syllable sitting low. (▁ khàawp drops low, then khun levels out flat and mid)
entries.headline: Khàawp-khun.
entries.scene: A Bangkok street corner in the rain. A traffic policeman in a white helmet holds out a battered leather wallet to a young woman, who has stopped mid-step and pressed her palms together in front of her face, head bowed, beaming.

entries.mnemonic: A cop hands back the wallet you dropped and you press your palms together: khàawp-khun. Stretch that cop out long — khàawp — and remember what the end of it is: khun, the ordinary Thai word for you. Thanking someone is literally handing them a you. (▁ khàawp sits low, then khun levels out flat)
entries.headline: khàawp-khun.
entries.scene: A uniformed Thai police officer on a busy pavement holds out a worn leather wallet to a young woman, who has stopped mid-step and raised both hands pressed together in front of her face, head bowed, smiling.

entries.mnemonic: A crow lands on a café table, caws once, then knocks the whole tote of pastries onto the pavement. It hops down beside the mess with its wings folded and its head bowed, apologising to the entire street. CAW plus TOTE: kǎaw-thôot, the bird with better manners than most. (↓ the voice drops on the second half, the bow of the head)
entries.headline: kǎaw-thôot.
entries.scene: A black crow stands head bowed, wings folded, beside an upended canvas tote with pastries scattered across wet pavement. A startled woman half rises from her café chair. Morning light on wet stone.

entries.mnemonic: A man backing out of a café swings his bag into a waiter and a whole rack of toast goes up in the air. On the sill a crow caws. Caw, toast. He turns round with both hands raised, wincing, saying it twice over: khǎaw-thôot. (↑ khǎaw climbs like the crow, then thôot drops as he bows)
entries.headline: Khǎaw-thôot!
entries.scene: The doorway of a small café. A man in a raincoat has just knocked a waiter's tray and slices of toast hang in the air around them both. He is turned back toward the waiter, shoulders hunched, both hands raised in apology, face screwed up.

entries.mnemonic: A glass lift climbs the outside of a tower and the numbers climb with it. Say KOON but grinning, lips pulled wide instead of pushed forward, and you land kʰɯ̂n: up, to rise, to increase. Prices do it, rivers do it, buses are boarded with it. (↓ falling, though everything in the scene is going up)
entries.headline: kʰɯ̂n!
entries.scene: A glass lift rising up the outside of a tall office tower, seen from below, with two passengers inside looking out and down. The city shrinks beneath them, rooftops and wires. Bright hazy sky, sun flaring off the glass.

entries.mnemonic: A man loads the car for the beach and stops short: a small nephew is already belted into the back seat with a towel round his neck. Dewey is coming too. dûai is the tag-along word — with, and also. (↓ falling, the voice drops as the boot slams)
entries.headline: …dûai.
entries.scene: A man in shorts leaning into the open rear door of a small car packed with beach gear, stopping short at the sight of a grinning boy already strapped into the back seat with a towel round his neck and a snorkel in one hand.

entries.mnemonic: A man called Jack turns up at the door with a battered suitcase plastered in shipping labels from a dozen countries. Where is he from? All of it. Jàak marks where a thing comes from — the starting point, never the destination. (▁ low and flat, a plain statement of origin)
entries.headline: jàak.
entries.scene: A traveller standing on a wooden doorstep at dusk with a battered leather suitcase bound in rope and worn straps, hat in hand, rain on his shoulders. The door is opening, warm light spilling onto him. A quiet street behind.

entries.mnemonic: A khan sits on a high seat above the works and watches: the digging, the hauling, the raising of beams. He does not care who swings the pick, only that the doing goes on. kaan is the doing itself, wrapped round a verb. (— flat and level, the work goes on unchanged)
entries.headline: kaan
entries.scene: A fur-robed chieftain seated on a raised timber platform on a hillside, arms folded, watching an enormous construction site below where hundreds of labourers dig, carry baskets of earth and raise timber frames. Dust, coloured pennants, low golden light.

entries.mnemonic: A woman steps up into the train, turns and waves — bye — and the doors close on her. Every leaving is a bye: bpai is to go, to head off, the direction away from where you are standing. (— flat and level, the wave held steady as the train pulls out)
entries.headline: bpai.
entries.scene: A woman standing in the open doorway of a departing train, one arm raised in a wave, bag over her shoulder. On the platform a small group waves back through the steam and motion blur. Overhead station lights, early morning.

entries.mnemonic: A vendor lifts a glass of orange tea and raises her eyebrows: this one? The customer nods once, hard. "Châi." Yes — chai, that is the one. (↓ falling, the voice drops with the nod)
entries.headline: Châi.
entries.scene: A morning tea cart where the vendor holds a tall glass of milky orange iced tea up across the counter, eyebrows raised in question, while the customer opposite nods once, firmly, finger already pointing at the glass. Ice bucket, steam, sunlit street.

entries.mnemonic: The same "my?" as ไหม — but shouted across a noisy bar, so the voice snaps up high and stays there instead of gliding. มั้ย is what friends say; ไหม is its polite written twin. (▲ high and flat-topped, a quick shout)
entries.headline: MY!
entries.scene: Crowded noisy Thai bar at night, packed with people. In the foreground a young man leans over a table, hands cupped around his mouth, shouting across the room toward a friend. The friend at the far side cups a hand behind his ear, squinting to hear.

entries.mnemonic: A grandmother stands at the top of the lane and calls one long flat syllable down it — "Maaa" — and every child in the street turns and starts walking towards her. The word that brings things to you. (— flat and level, the call holds one note)
entries.headline: Maaa—
entries.scene: An elderly Thai woman standing at the end of a narrow village lane with one hand cupped at her mouth, calling. Four children in school uniform at the far end have turned mid-play and are running back towards her.

entries.mnemonic: A train guard cannot remember a single passenger's name, so he just points and goes "choo" — lips pulled wide in a grin rather than pushed forward, which is exactly the Thai vowel. Chɯ̂ɯ is the name, the thing you are asked for first. (↓ falling, the voice drops as the name lands)
entries.headline: chɯ̂ɯ?
entries.scene: A uniformed train guard walking a crowded carriage, pointing cheerfully at one seated passenger after another, mouth stretched wide in an odd grin. Passengers grin back, baffled. Wooden seats, luggage racks, sunlight strobing through the windows.

entries.mnemonic: A landowner sweeps his arm over hills, rivers and villages running to the horizon: the whole estate. Take the tate off estate, put pra in front of it, and the estate has become a country. (↓ the second half falls hard, the arm sweeping down)
entries.headline: pra-tʰêet
entries.scene: A man in a wide hat standing on a high terrace with one arm sweeping across an enormous landscape of rice terraces, a winding river, distant temple spires and blue mountains fading to the horizon. Early morning haze, warm light.

entries.mnemonic: A gecko on a branch shoots its tongue out and the fly is gone. The tongue reaches, and it always gets there. Tʰɯ̌ng is arriving, reaching the place you were headed — and the point a thing extends to. (↑ rising, the flick goes up and out)
entries.headline: tʰɯ̌ng!
entries.scene: A green gecko clinging to a branch with its tongue shot out to full length toward a fly hovering just beyond, caught at the instant of contact. Broad tropical leaves, dappled light, shallow depth of field.

entries.mnemonic: A boy at the breakfast table tips the entire jar of orange Tang powder into one glass — not some of it, the lot. Tʰáng is the whole thing, both halves, every last one. (▲ high and taut, the voice stays up like the upended jar)
entries.headline: tʰáng!
entries.scene: A kitchen table at breakfast. A boy holds an enormous jar upside down over a single tall glass, orange powder pouring out and clouding the air around him. Cereal bowls forgotten. Morning light, curtains, an unimpressed cat on a chair.

entries.mnemonic: The cow lows exactly when the pail is set down, not a moment before. Say moo with the lips pulled wide in a grin instead of pushed forward and you have mɯ̂a: the word that marks the moment something happens. (↓ falling, the moo drops away at the end)
entries.headline: mɯ̂a…
entries.scene: A dairy shed at dawn. A farmer crouched on a low stool has just set a steel pail down under a cow, whose head is thrown back mid-bellow, mouth wide. Straw, a hanging lamp, cold blue light through the open door.

entries.mnemonic: A man sinks into a hammock and waves lazily — "sa-baaai" — a long drowsy bye as he drifts off. Nothing hurts, nothing to do. (— the second syllable stretches out level and relaxed)
entries.headline: sa-baaai…
entries.scene: A man lying back in a woven hammock strung between two coconut palms on a quiet Thai beach, one arm hanging loose and waving a slow lazy goodbye, eyes half closed, utterly relaxed. A cold drink rests in the sand beneath him. Calm turquoise sea and soft afternoon light behind.

entries.mnemonic: Two words already in the bag: thîi, the place, and yùu, to be living there. The place you live is your address. A postman holds up a parcel at the mouth of the lane and asks only that, and the whole street points at one gate. (▁ the second syllable settles low, fixed to the ground)
entries.headline: thîi-yùu?
entries.scene: A postman standing at the mouth of a narrow residential lane holding a brown parcel up in one hand. Four neighbours on doorsteps and balconies all point toward the same green gate further down. Washing lines, scooters, hot flat light.

entries.mnemonic: A road crew counts its men by the traffic cones on their heads: one cone, one man. Lose a cone and you have lost a person. khon is a person, and the word you count people with. (— flat and level, counting in an even voice)
entries.headline: One cone, one khon.
entries.scene: A row of road workers in orange vests standing to attention on a closed carriageway, each with a traffic cone upside down on his head like a hat, while a foreman walks the line pointing at each in turn.

entries.mnemonic: The contract is signed, everyone is smiling — but then the lawyer tears the last page clean off. Tɛ̀ɛ is that tear: everything before it stands, and what comes after changes it. Say it like 'tear' with the R swallowed. (▁ low and flat, the paper comes away without drama)
entries.headline: tɛ̀ɛ…
entries.scene: A boardroom. A lawyer stands at the head of the table calmly ripping the bottom sheet off a stapled contract, the torn strip already curling. Three people around the table, smiles frozen, one half out of a chair.

entries.mnemonic: A phone call in the middle of a market: where are you? The answer is one flat low word — yùu — and an arm goes straight up above the crowd so the caller can see where he is. yùu is being somewhere. (▁ low and flat, the voice sits still like the man)
entries.headline: …yùu.
entries.scene: A crowded night market seen from slightly above. One man stands motionless among the moving crowd with a phone to his ear and his free arm raised straight up, waving. Everyone else is blurred with movement. String lights, food steam.

entries.mnemonic: Someone asks the farmer what happened after the storm. He holds up an apple core, shrugs, and that is the answer: so, then, that is how it went. Kɔ̂ɔ is the small hinge between one thing and the next. (↓ falling, the shoulders come down with the voice)
entries.headline: kɔ̂ɔ…
entries.scene: A farmer standing in a wrecked orchard holding up a bare apple core between finger and thumb, shoulders lifted in a shrug. Snapped branches and scattered fruit across the mud behind him. Grey light after rain.

entries.mnemonic: Offer a Thai friend three restaurants and you will get kɔ̂ɔ-dâi — then-can, meaning any of them will do. It is the hinge word kɔ̂ɔ plus the can word dâi, delivered with the palms up. Agreement without enthusiasm, and it is everywhere. (↓ the second syllable drops, the shoulders drop with it)
entries.headline: kɔ̂ɔ dâi.
entries.scene: Three friends stopped on a street corner between three lit restaurant doorways. Two of them look expectantly at the third, who stands with both palms turned up and shoulders raised, entirely unbothered. Evening, neon reflections on wet pavement.

entries.mnemonic: A baker slaps a dark loaf on the counter and the customer stares at it: a rye? What is it? à-rai is the question you ask when you cannot name the thing in front of you. (— the second syllable levels out flat, eyebrows still up)
entries.headline: à-rai?
entries.scene: A bakery counter where the baker has just set down a dense dark loaf. The customer leans over it with head tilted and brow furrowed, one finger hovering above the crust without touching it.

entries.mnemonic: The place word thîi plus the knee of นี้ — this place. A man on a picnic blanket taps his own knee, then the grass right beside it: here, not over there, right at the knee. (↓ both syllables drop, each one planted)
entries.headline: thîi-nîi.
entries.scene: A man sitting cross-legged on a picnic blanket in a park, tapping his own knee with one hand and pressing his other flat on the grass beside the blanket. A friend standing a few metres away holds a basket, hesitating.

entries.mnemonic: Two hikers on a ridge; one points down at a hut in the valley where tea and a piece of nan bread are waiting. thîi is the place and nân is that one — thîi-nân, that place over there. (↓↓ both syllables drop, like the pointing arm)
entries.headline: thîi-nân.
entries.scene: Two hikers on a high rocky ridge at dusk, one with an arm fully outstretched pointing down into the valley at a tiny lit hut with smoke rising from it. Packs on their backs, wind in their jackets, layered mountains behind.

entries.mnemonic: A tea seller sets out two jars, one dark and one pale, and asks which yang you want. Every yin has its yang; every thing has its yàang — its sort, its kind, its type. (▁ low and flat, a plain sorting question)
entries.headline: yàang nǎi?
entries.scene: A tea seller behind a narrow counter with two open glass jars in front of her, one full of dark twisted leaves, one full of pale curled ones, holding a palm out over each.

entries.mnemonic: A man stops dead at the end of the high board, gripped by a qualm — nothing you can hold, but suddenly the whole matter is the size of the pool. khwaam turns a feeling into a thing: the -ness stuck on the front of a word. (— flat and level, the word gives nothing away)
entries.headline: khwaam…
entries.scene: A man standing frozen at the end of a high diving board, toes over the edge, arms half raised, staring down at the blue rectangle of water far below. Empty tiered seating all round, harsh poolside light, small ripples on the surface.

entries.mnemonic: Two baskets of flatbread on the counter. The customer waves off the near one and jabs a finger at the far basket — nán — that naan, the one over there. Níi is this; nán is that. (▲ high and taut, the finger jabs at arm's length)
entries.headline: nán!
entries.scene: A bakery counter with two wicker baskets of flatbread, one close and one at the far end. A customer leans across, waving one hand dismissively at the near basket while jabbing a finger at the far one.

entries.mnemonic: A man bites into a chewy sweet and his jaw locks shut. He waves both arms at the stall keeper, eyes wide, unable to get the word out — chûai, help me. (↓ falling, the cry drops away as his mouth clamps)
entries.headline: Chûai!
entries.scene: A man at a sweets stall with his jaw clamped shut on an enormous toffee, cheeks bulging, both arms waving frantically above his head, eyes wide with alarm. The stall keeper leans over trays of sticky sweets, laughing. Bright market awning, midday.

entries.mnemonic: The bartender fills the glass up to the red mark on its side and then keeps pouring. That mark is the limit; mâak is everything above it. Good, mâak. Hot, mâak. It is the word for too much of anything. (↓ falling, the pour keeps coming as the voice drops)
entries.headline: mâak!
entries.scene: A tall measuring glass on a bar with a red line ringing it partway up, liquid pouring over the rim and spreading across the counter. A bartender holds the bottle steady, looking straight at the viewer. Bottles behind, low amber light.

entries.mnemonic: The waiter whips the plate away the moment the last mouthful is gone — done, finished, lɛ́ɛo. Say the vowel in cat and slide it into ow. Everything that has already happened ends with it. (▲ high and taut, the plate snatched away)
entries.headline: …lɛ́ɛo!
entries.scene: A restaurant table where a waiter's hand is whipping an empty plate away just as the diner sets down his fork, the diner's other hand still half raised in surprise. Crumpled napkin, empty glass, warm evening light through a window.

entries.mnemonic: A baby cries somewhere in a dark house and every adult sits up in bed with the same question. Khrai sounds exactly like that cry, and the cry is always the question: whose baby, who is there, who did it. (— flat and level, the question sits in the middle)
entries.headline: khrai?
entries.scene: A dark bedroom, a couple sitting bolt upright in bed, both turned toward a half-open door with a strip of hallway light across the floor. Bedding thrown back, alarm clock on the nightstand. Deep blue night, one warm slice of light.

entries.mnemonic: ไหน and ไหม are twins with the same rising climb — only the first sound differs. ไหม (M) asks "is it so?"; ไหน (N) asks "where?". Picture two identical signposts at a fork: the M arm points at a question mark, the N arm points at a map. Same rise in the voice, different letter, different question. (↑ rising, the voice climbs as the eyes search)
entries.scene: A weathered wooden signpost at a fork in a dirt road in rural Thailand, with two identical arms pointing opposite ways. The left arm carries a large carved question mark; the right arm carries a small rolled map pinned to it.

entries.mnemonic: She asks for chilli and the cook reaches for the whole jar. "Nòi!" — voice dropping low as she pinches her fingers a centimetre apart. Just a bit. (▁ low and small, the voice shrinks with the gesture)
entries.headline: Nòi!
entries.scene: A street food stall. The cook, grinning, is tipping an enormous jar of dried red chilli flakes toward a bowl of noodles. Across the counter a woman lunges forward with one hand raised in alarm, her other hand pinching thumb and forefinger a tiny distance apart.

entries.mnemonic: At the end of the row the farmer tips the plough up and puts the question to the field: another furrow, or nothing? plàao means blank, empty — so rɯ̌ɯ-plàao is literally "or empty?", the yes-or-no bolted to the end of a sentence. (▁ the second word drops low, the plough set down)
entries.headline: …rɯ̌ɯ-plàao?
entries.scene: A farmer at the end of a half-ploughed paddy at sunset, one hand resting on the upturned handle of a wooden plough, looking back along the furrow. Half the field is turned dark earth, half is bare dry ground.

entries.mnemonic: The vendor names a price so small that the shopper has already walked off with the shirt. It took almost nothing. Thùuk is cheap — and, awkwardly for the learner, also correct. (▁ low and flat, a short blunt word for a short blunt price)
entries.headline: thùuk.
entries.scene: A clothes stall in a covered market. A shopper walks away with a folded shirt under his arm, already several steps gone, while the vendor stands with one open palm holding a single small coin. Hanging garments, strip lights, crowded aisle.

entries.english: to put in place; trust; to preserve
entries.mnemonic: She pushes the jars of pickled mango to the very back of the high shelf where nobody will get at them. Why keep so many? Because wái is exactly that — putting a thing aside to keep. (▲ high and taut, said over her shoulder)
entries.headline: …wái.
entries.scene: A woman on a step stool pushing a row of sealed glass jars of yellow pickled fruit to the very back of a high kitchen shelf, glancing back over her shoulder. The shelf is already crowded with jars.

entries.mnemonic: A kangaroo at a fork in the path, one carrot in each paw, head tilting from side to side and unable to settle it. Say 'roo' with the lips spread flat and you have rɯ̌ɯ — the little word that puts two things side by side: this, or that. (↑ rising, the voice tilts up like the head)
entries.headline: rɯ̌ɯ?
entries.scene: A kangaroo standing upright at a fork in a dusty path, a carrot held in each front paw, head tipped to one side. Two tracks lead away into dry scrub. Low sun, long shadows, red dust.

entries.mnemonic: Someone asks how he does it and the man taps his own chest with the butt of his cue: because he is a pro. That is the whole answer — prɔ́, the word that hands you the reason. (▲ high and taut, snapped out with the tap of the cue)
entries.headline: …prɔ́.
entries.scene: A snooker hall. A man in a waistcoat leans on his cue after a shot, tapping his own chest with two fingers, eyebrows raised, entirely unbothered. Onlookers round the table stare at the perfectly potted balls. Low hanging lamp, green baize, smoke.

entries.mnemonic: The two-tone siren says it over and over as the ambulance carves through traffic: way-laa, way-laa. Every second it loses is time somebody has not got. Weelaa is time itself — the hour, the while, the when. (— both syllables flat and even, the siren holding its note)
entries.headline: way-laa, way-laa
entries.scene: An ambulance cutting between stopped cars on a wet city street at night, blue light smeared across the windscreens around it. A clock tower stands lit above the rooftops behind. Rain, headlights, motion blur.

entries.mnemonic: A kangaroo in a quiz booth thumps the buzzer before the question is finished. The roo knows. rúu is knowing a fact, and this one knows the lot. (▲ high and taut, the buzzer's flat bright note)
entries.headline: Rúu!
entries.scene: A kangaroo sitting upright in a brightly lit television quiz booth, one paw slamming a big red buzzer, the other tucked smugly across its chest. Two human contestants in the neighbouring booths stare at it, mouths open. Studio lights, glossy desk.

entries.mnemonic: Twelve people round one table, all of them kin, every hand reaching into the same bowls at once. kin is what they are doing and who they are doing it with: you eat with your kin. One flat syllable, no fuss, used all day long. (— flat and level, an unhurried everyday word)
entries.headline: kin.
entries.scene: An extended Thai family crowded round a low table heaped with shared dishes, a dozen hands reaching in at once, a grandmother spooning rice into a small child's bowl, everyone talking over each other.

entries.mnemonic: A boy pulls up his shirt, pats a round full tummy and demands to know why he still has to finish the greens. Why this, why that — every one of his questions comes up out of that tummy, and none of them stops. tham-mai. (— both syllables flat and level, the drone of a child who will not give up)
entries.headline: tham-mai?
entries.scene: A small boy pats his bare round tummy, shirt pulled to his chin, mouth open mid-question, eyebrows high. Opposite him an exhausted parent slumps beside a plate of untouched greens. Warm evening kitchen.

entries.mnemonic: A tow truck is hauling your car away. You sprint after it shouting "How much?! — tâo-rài!" and the driver leans out and holds up a single loaf of rye bread: that's the price. TOW plus RYE, and you never forget asking what it costs. (↓ falls hard on tâo, then drops low again on rài)
entries.headline: tâo-rài?!
entries.scene: A yellow tow truck driving away down a city street with a small car hoisted on its hook. A man in office clothes sprints after it, briefcase flying open, one arm outstretched and mouth wide open mid-shout.

entries.mnemonic: The foreman watches the machine cough into life, sticks his thumb up, and the whole line starts moving. Tham is the doing word — make, do, get it done — and whatever the job is, the thumb settles it. (— flat and level, no fuss in it)
entries.headline: tham.
entries.scene: A factory floor. A foreman in a hard hat stands beside a starting conveyor with his thumb raised toward a control booth above. Workers along the line reach for the first parts coming through. Cold overhead lighting, oil-stained concrete.

entries.mnemonic: The foreman raises one thumb and the whole line starts moving — saws, hammers, sparks. Say thumb with a hard t and no lisp: tham, to make, to do. Thumb up and it gets made. (— flat and level, the same steady note as the machines)
entries.headline: tham!
entries.scene: A workshop foreman on a gantry above a busy production floor, one thumb raised high, mouth open in a shout. Below him men bend over benches, sparks flying from a grinder, timber moving along rollers. Shafts of dusty light from high windows.

entries.mnemonic: A woman comes to her back door and finds a hen where no hen should be: up on the kitchen table, mid-strut, among the breakfast plates. Her chin lifts as she says it — hěn, I see it. (↑ rising, the voice climbs with the eyebrows)
entries.headline: hěn!
entries.scene: A kitchen seen from the back doorway. A brown hen stands on the table stepping between plates and a teapot. A woman in the doorway has stopped dead, hands still on the door frame, chin up. Morning light across the floor tiles.

entries.mnemonic: The rain starts and the cow decides, against all precedent, to let herself into the kitchen. A whole cow through the doorway — khâo, to enter, to go in. (↓ falling, the voice drops as she ducks under the lintel)
entries.headline: Khâo.
entries.scene: A large brown cow halfway through the open back door of a village kitchen, head and shoulders inside, ducking under the low lintel, while a woman at the stove turns round with a wooden spoon raised.

entries.mnemonic: In the stairwell of an old hotel a chandelier hangs at every landing, one to a floor, each a little grander as you climb. Chán is the floor you are standing on — and, in a shop, the shelf. (▲ high and taut, said with the head tipped back)
entries.headline: chán.
entries.scene: Looking straight up a square hotel stairwell through four or five storeys of banisters, a lit chandelier hanging at each landing, the highest ones small with distance. Gilt, dust, warm bulbs against dark wood.

entries.mnemonic: The type word yàang plus rai, what: what way? A cook is asked how she gets the noodles to fly like that and simply holds her wrist up mid-toss. Yàang-rai is how — the manner of doing a thing. (— the second syllable levels out, the question left hanging)
entries.headline: yàang-rai?
entries.scene: A street kitchen. A cook holds a wok up and away from the flame with noodles and beansprouts in mid-air above it, her wrist cocked. An apprentice stares from the side, his own wok untouched. Night market lights, fire, steam.

entries.mnemonic: The family has moved into the barn and made it home: a bed in one stall, a kettle on a crate, washing strung between the beams. Say barn without the r — bâan — the house you live in. (↓ falling, the voice drops like a door closing for the night)
entries.headline: bâan.
entries.scene: The inside of a big timber barn made into a family home: a bed made up in one stall, a kettle steaming on a crate, laundry strung between the roof beams, a child playing on a rug on the straw floor.

entries.mnemonic: A farmer walks back across the field at dusk toward the one building with a light in it — the barn where everyone is waiting. Bâan is not the structure so much as the home inside it. (↓ falling, the voice settles the way he does)
entries.headline: bâan.
entries.scene: A farmer crossing a harvested field at dusk, silhouetted, tools over one shoulder, walking toward a low wooden house with one lit window and an open door. Hills and a fading orange sky behind. Long shadows across the stubble.

entries.mnemonic: He cannot get the sentence out, so he puts the words down one at a time like stones across a stream until they reach the far bank. Say put with a long oo: phûut, to speak. (↓ falling, each word dropped into place)
entries.headline: phûut.
entries.scene: A man crouched at the edge of a shallow stream placing flat stepping stones into the water one by one, a line of them already reaching halfway across to a woman waiting on the far bank. Morning mist, reeds, soft grey light.

entries.mnemonic: Given a mountain of vegetables to get through, the chef grins and reaches for the cleaver — chop, chop, chop, all afternoon — because this is the part of the job she likes. Chɔ̂ɔp is liking a thing enough to choose it. (↓ falling, the blade comes down with the voice)
entries.headline: chɔ̂ɔp!
entries.scene: A restaurant prep kitchen. A chef mid-swing with a heavy cleaver over a board heaped with spring onions, a vast crate of vegetables beside her, grinning. Chopped piles fan out across the steel counter. Steam and hard kitchen light.

entries.mnemonic: An old janitor lifts a keyring so heavy it needs both hands — hundreds of keys fanning out like a metal peacock. Someone asks the only sensible question: "Kìi?" How many keys? (▁ low and flat, a short blunt question)
entries.headline: Kìi?
entries.scene: An elderly janitor hoists an enormous iron keyring with both hands, hundreds of keys fanned out in a glinting spray. A student beside him stares up, counting. Dim school corridor, shafts of window light.

entries.mnemonic: A cow leans over the fence into the neighbour's rye field and moos, while the farmer stands beside it with his watch open, waiting on the crop. Moo, rye. mûuea-rài asks the only thing either of them wants to know: when. Say MOO with the lips pulled wide instead of pushed forward and the Thai vowel lands. (↓ mûuea drops, then rài falls away low)
entries.headline: mûuea-rài?
entries.scene: A brown cow with its head stretched over a wooden fence into a tall golden field of rye, mouth open mid-bellow.

entries.mnemonic: The choirmaster stops the choir to fix the line which they have just sung — and that little 'which' is the word. Say SUNG with the lips spread flat instead of rounded and you have sɯ̂ng: the joiner that hooks a description onto whatever came before. (↓ falling, the voice drops as the clause attaches)
entries.headline: sɯ̂ng…
entries.scene: A choirmaster with one hand raised flat, having just cut off a choir mid-phrase; thirty singers stand with mouths still open. A church hall, high windows, folded music stands. Cool daylight from above.

entries.mnemonic: A road crew stands over a steaming bucket of tar with the rain coming in. If they pour now it sets; if they wait they lose the day. Everything hangs on that if — thâa, said like 'tar' with the R swallowed. (↓ falling, the word drops like the first raindrop)
entries.headline: thâa…
entries.scene: Three road workers in overalls standing around a steaming black tar bucket on a half-finished stretch of road, all looking up at a bank of dark cloud rolling in. Rollers and cones behind them. First drops darkening the asphalt.

entries.mnemonic: The tailor runs the tape round the customer and calls the number out: one body, measured. tuua is the body itself, and the word you count animals and bodies with — two arms, two legs, one tuua. (— flat and level, the tape held straight)
entries.headline: …tuua.
entries.scene: A tailor kneeling to run a cloth tape measure round the waist of a customer standing on a low wooden box with both arms held straight out, pins gripped in the tailor's lips.

entries.mnemonic: nák- is the prefix Thai sticks on the front of anyone who does a thing. Hear it as a knack — the boy with a knack for it — and glue it to riian, to study. Knack for studying: a student. Learn nák- once and it hands you a dozen other people. (— riian levels out flat and patient at the end)
entries.scene: A Thai schoolboy in a crisp white uniform sits at a wooden classroom desk, effortlessly spinning a globe on one fingertip while his classmates twist round in their seats to watch, delighted. Morning sun through louvred shutters, dust hanging in the light.

entries.mnemonic: The stall keeps the same leaves and pours a third round from them, because nothing here is finished until it cannot be used again. Chái is to use — to put a thing to work. (▲ high and taut, a brisk working word)
entries.headline: chái.
entries.scene: A roadside tea stall. A vendor pours from a battered dented pot into a glass, the spent leaves heaped in a strainer beside her, three used glasses waiting. Close crop on hands and steam, sunlit street beyond.

entries.mnemonic: A boy at the zoo railing points at the yak and will not be moved: he wants it, wants to take it home. jàak is wanting — a long low ache of a word with a yak at the end of it. (▁ low and flat, the want settles in and stays)
entries.headline: jàak…
entries.scene: A small boy gripping a zoo railing with both hands, cheek pressed between the bars, staring longingly at a huge shaggy yak chewing in its enclosure. His mother tugs gently at his hood from behind. Grey overcast light, damp ground.

entries.mnemonic: A mare stands square over her foal in the paddock and will not let anyone past her shoulder. Say 'mare' with the R swallowed and you have mɛ̂ɛ — mother, and the first word a Thai child shouts. (↓ falling, the voice drops warm and final)
entries.headline: mɛ̂ɛ.
entries.scene: A chestnut mare standing broadside over a folded-up foal in wet paddock grass, ears back, head turned toward the fence. A figure at the gate has stopped with one hand on the latch. Morning mist, low sun.

entries.mnemonic: A small boy grabs an enormous weathered hand — a bear's paw of a hand — and says "Phôo." The hand belongs to his father, and it swallows his whole fist. (↓ falling, warm and settled)
entries.headline: Phôo.
entries.scene: Close view of a small boy's hand gripping the huge weathered calloused hand of his father, whose forearm fills the frame. The boy, about five, looks up with total trust; the father, a broad Thai labourer in a faded work shirt, looks down at him with a quiet smile.

entries.mnemonic: A cow has got her whole head into the rice cauldron and will not come out. Grains fly across the kitchen floor. The farmer's voice comes down hard — khâao! — because that is his rice, a month of it, and a cow is eating it. (↓ falling, the shout drops out of him as he lunges)
entries.headline: Khâao!
entries.scene: A cow has pushed her head deep into an enormous cauldron of white rice, grains scattered over the floor. A farmer in a straw hat lunges at her, both arms raised. Morning light through a slatted window.

entries.mnemonic: A man raises his glass and intones "dɯɯm…" like a funeral bell — the last drink before DOOM. The trick is the lips: say DOOM while grinning, lips pulled wide instead of pushed forward, and you land the Thai vowel exactly. (▁ low and heavy, like the glass coming back down on the table)
entries.headline: dɯɯm…
entries.scene: A lone man at a long empty banquet table in a candlelit hall, raising a heavy glass in a solemn toast, grinning oddly wide as he does it. Behind him a huge cracked bronze bell hangs in the shadows. Guttering candles, long shadows, a sense of last things.

entries.mnemonic: He plunges both hands into the mountain stream and they go numb in seconds, that shocking cold where the fingers stop belonging to you. náam is water, and water this cold numbs. Short and high, up where the gasp is. (▲ high and taut, the sound of breath sucked in)
entries.headline: náam!
entries.scene: A young man crouched at the edge of a fast mountain stream, both hands submerged to the wrist in clear rushing water, face screwed up and mouth open in a gasp.

entries.mnemonic: A fortune teller peers over her cards, jabs a finger across the table and says "Ah — YOU!" She has guessed your age to the year, and the YOU comes out bright and hard and stays up there. aa-yú is the number of years you have. (▲ the second syllable snaps up high on YOU and holds)
entries.headline: Ah — YOU!
entries.scene: A fortune teller's booth draped in red cloth. An old woman with rings on every finger leans across a spread of cards and jabs one finger directly at the viewer, eyes wide with certainty.

entries.mnemonic: A drummer walks down the lane beating a tom-tom and by the end of it every child in the village has fallen in behind him, matching his step. Taam is to follow — a person, a road, or a rule. (— flat and even, like the beat he keeps)
entries.headline: taam!
entries.scene: A drummer walking away down a narrow village lane with a tom-tom strapped at his hip, a straggling line of small children following in step behind him. Wooden houses, chickens scattering, dust and warm afternoon light.

entries.mnemonic: Hum an ng in the nose, then say earn: ngɤɤn. Old money was silver, so the same word does both jobs — the dull silver coins counted out of a pay packet at the end of the week are what you earned. (— flat and level, one coin, one note)
entries.headline: ngɤɤn.
entries.scene: A pair of hands counting old silver coins out of a small cloth pay packet onto a worn wooden table, a short stack already built beside them. A rolled shirt cuff, dim window light behind, dust in the air.

entries.mnemonic: Stick a hum on the front of 'earn' and you have it: ngɤɤn. At closing time the stallholder counts the day's takings into a biscuit tin, note by note. What she earned is what the word means — money, and silver before that. (— flat and level, coin after coin)
entries.headline: ngɤɤn.
entries.scene: A market stall after closing, shutters half down. A woman sits on a stool counting banknotes into a battered biscuit tin on her lap, coins stacked on the counter beside her. One hanging bulb, everything else dark.

entries.mnemonic: Hum an ng in the nose, then say earn — ngɤɤn, the money you earn. Notes counted onto the tray one at a time; the same word whether it is coins, notes or a salary. (— flat and level, an even count)
entries.headline: ngɤɤn.
entries.scene: A market trader's hands counting banknotes one by one from a fat roll onto a metal tray on the counter, a queue of customers waiting beyond. Overhead strip light, produce crates stacked behind, late afternoon.

entries.mnemonic: A row of balloons tied along a fence, and only some of them go bang — three burst, the rest hang there untouched. Baang is exactly that: some, certain ones, not all of them. (— flat and level, no drama in the word itself)
entries.headline: baang.
entries.scene: A garden fence strung with a row of party balloons, three of them burst into curls of rubber on their strings, the rest still full and bobbing. Trestle table with paper cups behind. Bright afternoon, grass, no people.

entries.mnemonic: A mouse crosses the kitchen floor and the cook shrieks — eek — then another, then another. Each one gets its own eek. ʔìik is more: again, another one. (▁ low and flat, and by the third mouse the eek has gone tired)
entries.headline: …ʔìik.
entries.scene: A cook standing on a kitchen chair with her apron gathered in both fists, looking down at three mice crossing the tiled floor in single file, her expression more weary than frightened. Copper pans, a pot left steaming on the stove.

entries.mnemonic: Do plus give: tham (to do) and hâi (to give). A father tickles a baby until she shrieks with laughter — he did something, and it gave her the laugh. That is the whole word: this made that happen. (↓ the second syllable drops, the handing-over)
entries.headline: tham-hâi.
entries.scene: A father sitting on the floor with a baby lying across his knees, both hands tickling her ribs, both of them mid-laugh with eyes screwed shut. Sunlit living room, scattered toys, curtains moving.

entries.mnemonic: A boy snatches a roasting chestnut straight off the brazier — ow — and hangs on to it anyway, because he wants it. Ao is wanting and taking in one syllable, and the vendor will throw it at you as a question. (— flat and level, said fast)
entries.headline: ao!
entries.scene: A street brazier of chestnuts glowing over coals. A small boy has just grabbed one and is shaking his hand in the air, chestnut clamped in his fingers, face screwed up. The vendor leans back laughing. Night, sparks, orange light.

entries.mnemonic: A father hoists a toddler onto his shoulders and answers the neighbour's question with one word: his lûuk. Say Luke and let the voice fall — your child, and the young of anything. (↓ falling, the voice drops as the boy is swung up)
entries.headline: …lûuk.
entries.scene: A father in a village lane swinging a laughing toddler up onto his shoulders, both hands round the child's ankles, while a neighbour leans over a low fence smiling. Chickens scattering, washing on a line, late golden light.

entries.mnemonic: He carries her rucksack as well as his own up every step of the hill and will not hand either back. The first sound of rucksack is rák: love, done rather than said. (▲ high and taut, said through the effort)
entries.headline: rák.
entries.scene: A young man toiling up a long flight of temple steps with two large rucksacks, one on his back and one across his front, sweat on his face, while a young woman climbs easily beside him with empty hands, laughing.

entries.mnemonic: The hunter presses his ear flat to the coffin lid with the fangs an inch away on the other side. Listening is the entire job. Fang is to listen, and it is the English word unchanged. (— flat and level, held completely still)
entries.headline: fang.
entries.scene: A stone crypt lit by one candle. A man kneels with his ear pressed against the lid of a heavy wooden coffin, eyes wide, both palms flat on the wood. Cobwebs, damp walls, a single flame.

entries.mnemonic: Two brothers stand back to back to settle who is taller. The taller one is P — top of the list — "Phîi" — and his hand comes down flat on his brother's head to prove it. (↓ falling, the hand settles the matter)
entries.headline: Phîi.
entries.scene: Two Thai brothers standing back to back in a living room, comparing heights. The taller older one has reached up and over to lay his hand flat on top of his younger brother's head, smirking. The younger one stands on tiptoe, scowling, arms folded.

entries.mnemonic: The little one pipes up — "Nóng!" — high and bright, the small voice that always goes up at the end and always wants in. He is the one still waiting to grow. (▲ high, a small bright voice)
entries.headline: Nóng!
entries.scene: A small child jumping up with one arm stretched high, beaming, trying to be included in a group of older kids who are standing in a huddle above him. He is clearly the smallest by a head. Sunlit Thai schoolyard, dusty ground, green trees behind.

entries.mnemonic: The diver hesitates on the rock and her friend flicks a hand at the water: go on, see, just jump. sì is that flick — the little push on the end of an order that turns it into encouragement. (▁ low and clipped, over before it starts)
entries.headline: …sì!
entries.scene: Two teenagers on a river rock in swimwear; one stands at the edge with arms wrapped round herself, the other sits behind flicking an open hand towards the green water below, grinning. Jungle bank, sun flashing on the water.

entries.mnemonic: Three friends order; two have chosen and the third is still reading. The waitress turns to her with one eyebrow up and a single syllable: khun lâ — and you? Lâ is the nudge that throws the question back at someone. (↓ falling, the voice drops as the eyebrow goes up)
entries.headline: khun lâ?
entries.scene: A restaurant table of three. A waitress with a notepad has turned to the last diner, pen poised, one eyebrow raised. Two friends watch the third, who is still hidden behind a tall folded card held up to her face.

entries.mnemonic: Someone tells you something you flatly do not believe and all you can manage is a rising grunt — rə̌ə? It is the vowel of English er with an r on the front and the voice climbing. The eyebrows do the rest. (↑ rising, voice and eyebrows climb together)
entries.headline: Rə̌ə?
entries.scene: Two women at a café table; one leans back with both eyebrows shot up and her chin tucked in, staring at the other, who is still talking with her hands mid-gesture. Half-drunk iced coffees, condensation rings on the table, bright window light.

entries.mnemonic: A baker's tray of identical round baps with one plaited loaf among them — a different bɛ̀ɛp, the same dough. Bɛ̀ɛp is the model, the kind, the way a thing is made or worn. (▁ low and flat, a plain word for a plain thing)
entries.headline: bɛ̀ɛp nǎi?
entries.scene: A bakery window tray packed with identical round bread rolls, one plaited loaf sitting among them, slightly larger. Flour on the tray, tongs resting on the edge, a child's face reflected in the glass. Morning light.

entries.mnemonic: An orc is thrown out of the tavern and lands in the street — out, and staying out. ɔ̀ɔk is going out: the exit, the way out, the thing that leaves. (▁ low and flat, the sound of the door shutting behind him)
entries.headline: ʔɔ̀ɔk!
entries.scene: A heavy tavern door swinging shut while a large green-skinned brute in patched leather sits stunned in the muddy street outside, his helmet rolling away. A pair of hands still visible at the doorframe. Lantern light spilling out, wet cobbles, night.

entries.mnemonic: The place word thîi plus sùt, the end: the point right at the end of the line. A sweep climbs out on top of the tallest chimney in the city, black with soot, every other stack below him. The most, the -est of anything. (▁ the last syllable drops low and stops)
entries.headline: thîi-sùt.
entries.scene: A chimney sweep sitting astride the rim of the tallest brick chimney above a city of smaller stacks and rooftops, soot-blackened, brushes slung on his back. Smoke drifting below him. Cold dawn, pale sky.

entries.mnemonic: A proper row over the garden fence: one family on this side, one on that, and every second word is us — us, we, our lot. rao is we, and it sounds like the row itself. (— flat and level, both sides holding the same note)
entries.headline: rao.
entries.scene: Two families leaning over a low garden fence at each other, arms thrown wide, mouths open mid-shout, each group pressed shoulder to shoulder on its own side. Washing lines, scattered toys, hot bright afternoon.

entries.mnemonic: Every cake on the stand sits on its own lace doily, and each doily was cut by hand by the woman behind the counter — made by her. Dooi is the by-word: done by, through, by means of. (— flat and level, a quiet credit)
entries.headline: dooi.
entries.scene: A glass-fronted cake stand. A woman's hands lower a small iced cake onto a white lace doily on the top shelf, a stack of cut doilies beside her. Scissors and paper scraps on the counter. Bright shop light.

entries.mnemonic: A man upends the entire sofa hunting for his keys, and when they finally drop out of the frame he says the word itself — hǎa. The looking and the finding share one sound. (↑ rising, the voice climbs the longer the search goes on)
entries.headline: hǎa!
entries.scene: A living room turned over: a sofa tipped upside down, cushions everywhere, a man on his knees underneath it with one arm out to catch a set of keys falling from the frame. Lamp knocked sideways, evening light.

entries.mnemonic: One engine still running on an empty airfield long after everything else has shut down, alone out there in the dark. ʔeeng tacks itself onto a person and means by themselves: he did it eeng, he alone. (— flat and level, the engine holding one note)
entries.headline: …ʔeeng.
entries.scene: A single small propeller aircraft on a vast empty airfield at dusk with its propeller spinning and navigation lights on, every other aircraft in the row dark and chocked. Long shadows, orange horizon, nobody in sight.

entries.mnemonic: One hen finds the split feed sack and immediately tells the whole yard about it — bawk, bawk, bawk — until every bird in the place is running. Bɔ̀ɔk is to tell: news, instructions, or the truth. (▁ low and flat, a plain announcement)
entries.headline: bɔ̀ɔk.
entries.scene: A farmyard. One hen stands on a burst sack of grain with her beak open mid-squawk, wings half spread, while a dozen other hens sprint toward her from every corner. Spilled feed, straw, hard morning light.

entries.mnemonic: A man who sued for damages settles out of court and has spent the cheque by the afternoon. Say 'sue' with the lips pulled wide instead of pushed forward and you land sɯ́ɯ — to buy. (▲ high and taut, the word snaps up like a price)
entries.headline: sɯ́ɯ!
entries.scene: A man in a crumpled suit walking down courthouse steps loaded with shopping bags in both hands, a new hat on, grinning. Pigeons, columns, other people in suits going the other way. Bright midday.

entries.mnemonic: Halfway across the tarmac the traveller stops, turns to the ground crew and asks which way the gate is — tǎam — the voice climbing the way every question climbs. Take the tarm off tarmac and you have the Thai for ask. (↑ rising, the voice climbs like a hand going up)
entries.headline: Tǎam?
entries.scene: An airport apron at dusk. A traveller with a wheeled case has halted mid-stride on wet tarmac and turned to a ground marshal in a hi-vis vest, palms open in a questioning gesture. The marshal points away toward distant terminal lights.

entries.mnemonic: It is noon and nothing is happening. He lies flat and the afternoon goes on and on — "nooon" — never rising, never falling. (— completely level; the voice lies down too)
entries.headline: nooon…
entries.scene: A man asleep flat on his back on a wooden bench under a shop awning in the middle of a blazing hot day, hat over his face, one arm hanging off the side. A wall clock behind him has both hands pointing straight up. Empty sun-bleached street, hard midday shadows, heat haze.

entries.mnemonic: You suggest something ridiculous. Your friend shakes her head once and sets a heavy rock down on the table between you. Solid as a rock: no, definitely not, don't even think it. (▁ low and flat, the last word on the matter)
entries.headline: …ròok.
entries.scene: Two friends at a small café table. One leans forward mid-sentence, hands open, pleading. The other has just set a heavy grey river stone down on the tabletop between them with a thud, and is shaking her head once, eyebrows raised, utterly unmoved. Coffee cups rattle slightly.

entries.mnemonic: A chef scans a row of identical mangoes, then slaps one down on the board — "nîi lɛ̀!" — that one. The word is over before it starts, cut off short like the slap itself. (▁ low and clipped, stopped dead at the end)
entries.headline: …lɛ̀!
entries.scene: A market chef's hands above a wooden board, having just slapped one mango down hard onto it; the other identical mangoes are lined up untouched behind. Slight motion blur on the striking hand, a puff of disturbed flour or dust rising from the board. Overhead market lighting, close crop.

entries.mnemonic: A woodsman too hungry to wait for the fire swings his hatchet and hews a slice straight off the ham hanging in the smokehouse, chewing while he cuts. Hew first, cook later. hǐu is the hunger that will not sit down and be patient. (↑ rising, the voice climbs like a stomach complaining)
entries.headline: hǐu!
entries.scene: A ragged woodsman swings a hatchet into an enormous smoked ham hanging from a rafter, a thick slice dropping into his other hand, cheeks bulging as he chews. A dim smokehouse, smoky shafts of light.

entries.mnemonic: Four friends outside a karaoke bar and one of them still hesitating on the step. The others tug his sleeve: pai thə̀ — go on, let's. It is the softest possible shove, the syllable that turns an order into a let's. (▁ low and short, gone almost before it starts)
entries.headline: pai thə̀!
entries.scene: A neon karaoke doorway at night. Three young people have hold of a fourth by the sleeve and elbow, hauling him laughing toward the entrance while he leans back. Wet pavement, reflected neon, scooters parked along the kerb.

entries.mnemonic: The same see as สิ, but snapped out high and quick between friends — and the hand on your back is harder. สิ nudges; ซิ shoves. Go on, do it. (▲ high and taut, a short bright shove)
entries.headline: …sí!
entries.scene: A boy on the edge of a wooden jetty with both arms out for balance, another boy behind him with both palms planted flat between his shoulder blades, laughing and pushing. River water below, a moored longtail boat beyond, hot midday light.

entries.mnemonic: The one Thai particle that translates itself: jâ is ja, the German yes, and it carries the same warm agreement — an aunt answering a small child, a friend saying of course. Women use it where the conversation is friendly rather than formal. (↓ falling, warm and settled)
entries.headline: jâ.
entries.scene: A kitchen doorway. An aunt in an apron leans down nodding at a small child who is holding up an empty bowl with both hands. Steam from a pot behind her, worn tiles, warm afternoon light.

entries.mnemonic: A boy carries an old woman's shopping across the road and walks off before she can thank him — a good deed. Take the d off the end and you have dii: good. (— flat and level, said without fuss)
entries.headline: dii.
entries.scene: A teenage boy setting two heavy shopping bags down on a kerb beside an elderly woman and already turning away with a hand half raised, while she reaches after him. Busy street behind, traffic, warm late light.

entries.mnemonic: One letter short of เพื่อน, friend — and that is the sense: pʰɯ̂a is doing a thing for somebody, and adding the n gives you the person you do it for. The vowel is the hard part: start at 'oo' with the lips spread flat and let it fall away into 'ah'. (↓ falling, the voice drops like something handed over)
entries.headline: pʰɯ̂a khun.
entries.scene: Two women walking a rainy street under one umbrella, the nearer one holding it entirely over her friend so that her own shoulder and sleeve are soaked through. Puddles, passing headlights, evening.

entries.mnemonic: A player pulls the one block holding the whole tower up; therefore — and it is a proper therefore — it comes down across the table. Take the first sound of Jenga and say it with the lips spread flat: tɕɯng. (— flat and level, said into the silence after the crash)
entries.headline: tɕɯng.
entries.scene: A wooden block tower collapsing across a table, blocks tumbling and bouncing, a young woman's hand frozen in the air still holding the single block she pulled, her face caught between horror and laughter. Friends leaning back, drinks, warm lamplight.

entries.mnemonic: Take STRONG and knock the S off the front: troŋ. A soldier marches dead straight down a painted line, jaw set, refusing to deviate an inch. Strong and straight are the same idea here. (— flat and level, like the line he is walking)
entries.headline: troŋ!
entries.scene: A soldier in parade uniform marching precisely along a freshly painted white line down the centre of a wide road, back rigid, gaze fixed dead ahead. The line runs away from him to a vanishing point. Onlookers stand well back on both kerbs. Bright hard sunlight, sharp shadows.

entries.mnemonic: A rope tore in two and the sailor splices the ends back together, turn by turn, one length carried on into the next. tɔ̀ɔ is joining on: continue, connect, and so much each. (▁ low and flat, the steady pull of the splice)
entries.headline: tɔ̀ɔ…
entries.scene: Close view of a sailor's weathered hands splicing two frayed rope ends together on a boat deck, the strands interwoven halfway, a marlinspike gripped in his teeth. Coiled rope, wet planks, bright sea glare behind.

entries.mnemonic: A temple bell is struck once for every year of the old abbot's life, and a novice keeps count with knots in a cord — each time it rang, one more knot. Khráng is that: a time, an occasion, once. (▲ high and taut, the note hanging in the air)
entries.headline: khráng.
entries.scene: A young monk standing beside a huge bronze temple bell, a knotted cord looped through his fingers, the swinging beam just leaving the bell's rim. Other monks watching from the steps. Early gold light, incense smoke.

entries.mnemonic: A shopkeeper slaps a fat red starburst over the old one in the window and a LOT has come off. lót is the cut itself — prices, speed, weight, volume, anything that comes down — but the voice does not come down with it. It snaps up bright and stays up. (▲ high and taut, called over his shoulder from the step stool)
entries.headline: lót!
entries.scene: A grinning shopkeeper on a step stool inside a shopfront window, pressing a huge red starburst sticker over a smaller one on the glass, the corner of the old one still peeling up. Shoppers outside press in to look.

entries.mnemonic: A rented room in a Hong Kong tower block, so small that a man standing in the middle of it reaches both walls without straightening his arms. Hong, hâawng: the room. This one is all the room there is, and the voice drops like the ceiling. (↓ falling, heavy and low)
entries.headline: hâawng.
entries.scene: A tiny high-rise flat. A man stands in the centre with both arms half raised, palms flat against opposite walls, a folded bed and a single hotplate crammed in behind him.

entries.mnemonic: Ask a Thai shopkeeper what she does and she will tell you she runs this place. A ráan is a shop — the thing you run. The word and the job are the same sound. (▲ high, said with pride)
entries.headline: My ráan.
entries.scene: A proud middle-aged Thai woman standing in the open doorway of her small neighbourhood shop, arms folded, chin up, framed by shelves of goods stacked floor to ceiling behind her. A painted awning above the door, a scooter parked outside, early morning light down the street.

entries.mnemonic: Knock the P off PRAWN and you have ráawn. A fat prawn hits the grill bars and hisses, and the cook snatches his fingers back out of the flame with a yelp. Hot — the thing itself and the complaint about it, in one word. (▲ high and taut, the yelp of a burnt finger)
entries.headline: Ráawn!
entries.scene: Close on a charcoal grill at a night market: a fat prawn just dropped onto the glowing bars, flames curling up around its shell, the cook's hand jerking back with fingers splayed, his face screwed up mid-wince. Sparks, smoke, deep night behind.

entries.mnemonic: Take PRAWN and knock the P off the front: ráawn. The cook flicks prawns onto a grill so fierce they curl and hiss the instant they land, and his hand snaps back from the bars with his fingers splayed. Everything about that grill is the word. (▲ high and taut, a yelp pitched at the top of the voice)
entries.headline: ráawn!
entries.scene: A street cook flicks prawns onto a blazing charcoal grill; they curl in a burst of flame and steam as his hand jerks back, fingers splayed, face screwed up. Night market, orange firelight.

entries.mnemonic: A single yen coin has been left in the freezer overnight and comes out furred with white frost, so cold it sticks to the fingertips that lift it. yen is cold, and the temperature never shifts while the voice holds it. (— flat and level, the cold does not move)
entries.headline: yen.
entries.scene: A close view of a hand holding a small coin, its face lost under white frost, fingertips pink and stuck to its surface, cold vapour spilling down from an open freezer behind.

entries.mnemonic: You jàai for your chai. The two words sit almost on top of each other — the drink and the paying for it — so every cup you buy is a free rehearsal. (▁ low, the flat sound of coins going down on the counter)
entries.headline: jàai for chai.
entries.scene: A tea stall counter. A customer's hand places a small stack of coins down on the wooden counter beside a steaming glass of milky orange Thai iced tea. The vendor's hand is reaching for the coins from the other side. Close low-angle crop on the counter, warm steam, sunlit street behind.

entries.mnemonic: One spoonful and the man at the counter shuts his eyes, presses a hand flat to his chest and cannot say anything at all except à-rɔ̀y. The cook everyone on the street calls Roy points at him with the tongs. A Roy, and a review that needs no words. (▁ low, the voice drops as the eyes close)
entries.headline: à-rɔ̀y…
entries.scene: A diner at a stall counter sits with eyes squeezed shut, one hand pressed to his chest, spoon still in his mouth, bowl emptied. The grinning cook points at him with tongs. Wok flame, warm bulbs.

entries.mnemonic: Take royal and drop the -al: a-roy. A king in full robes has folded himself onto a plastic stool at a noodle cart, taken one mouthful and closed his eyes. The royal verdict on street food, and the whole court leaning in to watch him give it. (▁ the last syllable drops low and satisfied)
entries.headline: à-ròi!
entries.scene: A king in an embroidered robe and gold circlet perched on a low plastic stool at a night-market noodle cart, eyes closed in bliss, a laden spoon halfway to his mouth. The vendor grins over her steaming pot; two courtiers in uniform wait awkwardly behind.

entries.mnemonic: Asked whether the mangoes will be ripe by Friday, the farmer looks up at the tree, tips his hand from side to side and says máng — probably, don't hold me to it. The first syllable of mango, thrown up high. (▲ high, the voice lifts and leaves it open)
entries.headline: máng.
entries.scene: A mango orchard. A farmer stands under a heavy tree of half-ripe fruit, one hand tipping side to side at chest height, squinting up. A buyer beside him with an empty crate waits. Hot hazy light through leaves.

entries.mnemonic: The same cow as เข้า, at a different pitch: this one climbs. Asked who left the gate open, the farmer just lifts his chin at the man leaning on it — khǎo, him. (↑ rising, the chin and the voice go up together)
entries.headline: Khǎo.
entries.scene: A farmer standing in a yard with arms folded, lifting his chin towards a sheepish young man leaning on an open gate, while a cow wanders out through it behind him. Muddy yard, wooden fence, flat morning light.

entries.mnemonic: One lie needs a second one to prop it up, and that one needs three more. By midnight he has lǎai of them — many, more than he can keep straight. (↑ rising, the voice climbs with the pile)
entries.headline: lǎai.
entries.scene: A man sitting on the edge of his bed in the small hours, head in his hands, the floor around him buried under a huge drift of crumpled paper balls. One lamp, curtains drawn, everything else dark.

entries.mnemonic: The grand pooh-bah arrives: sash, medals, and a chair carried by four straining men. phûu is the one-who — put it in front of a trade and you have the person who does it. (↓ falling, the voice drops with the weight of the title)
entries.headline: phûu…
entries.scene: A pompous official in a sash heavy with medals being carried through a crowd on an ornate chair by four straining bearers, chin high, one hand raised in a small wave. Coloured pennants, dust, bright ceremonial daylight.

entries.mnemonic: A tray of sweets goes round the classroom and each child takes exactly one — took, took, took, all the way along the row. Thúk is every and each, one at a time, and it is short: took, not toooook. (▲ high and taut, clipped off)
entries.headline: thúk khon.
entries.scene: A classroom row seen along its length: a tray of wrapped sweets being passed hand to hand, each child holding one already, the last two reaching. Wooden desks, uniforms, sunlight through louvred windows.

entries.mnemonic: The twin of หน่อย, but the voice stays up high. A boy holds the bag upside down over his palm: one chilli left, nɔ́ɔi, that is all there is. (▲ high and taut, held up like the chilli itself)
entries.headline: nɔ́ɔi.
entries.scene: A boy holding a nearly empty paper bag upside down over his open palm with a single small red chilli sitting in it, arm raised so a woman at a stove can see.

entries.mnemonic: Point at the line snaking along the railings outside the embassy and ask what it is: that is a queue. Say 'queue' with the lips spread flat rather than pushed forward and you have kʰɯɯ — the equals sign of Thai: this is that. (— flat and level, stating a fact)
entries.headline: khɯɯ…
entries.scene: A long queue of people along iron railings outside a grand stone building, doubling back on itself. A newcomer stands at the end pointing along it with a puzzled expression. Grey morning, coats, bags.

entries.mnemonic: The night watchman stops dead on the stair — hark, if that was a footstep, someone is in the house. hàak is the if that opens the sentence: everything hangs on what he hears next. (▁ low and flat, said under the breath)
entries.headline: hàak…
entries.scene: A night watchman frozen halfway up a dark wooden staircase, lantern lowered, head turned to listen, one foot still raised above the next step. Long shadows up the wall, a half-open door above him, faint moonlight.

entries.mnemonic: A green shoot breaks the crust of a cracked field: everything that is born comes up out of the dirt. Gɤ̀ɤt rhymes with dirt with a hard G on the front — to be born, to arise, to happen at all. (▁ low and flat, the first quiet moment of a life)
entries.headline: gɤ̀ɤt.
entries.scene: Close view of a single green seedling pushing up through hard cracked earth, soil crumbs lifted on its bent head. A wide dry field blurred behind. First light, long low shadows.

entries.mnemonic: An old man keeps a jar on the sill and drops one dried pea into it every birthday. The jar is nearly full. pii is a year — count the peas and you have his age. (— flat and level, one pea, one note)
entries.headline: …pii.
entries.scene: An old man's hands dropping a single dried pea into a tall glass jar almost full of them on a windowsill, beside a slice of cake with one candle burning. Warm low sunlight through the window, a faded curtain.

entries.mnemonic: Put a hum in front of 'naan' and you have it. The baker slaps flatbread onto the oven wall all night — this is his ngaan, his work. A wedding or a fair is a ngaan too: any event people work at. (— flat and level, the same all shift)
entries.headline: ngaan.
entries.scene: A tandoor oven glowing with coals, a baker leaning in to slap a disc of dough against the hot clay wall, several breads already stuck and blistering. Bare arms, flour, sweat, deep night behind him.

entries.mnemonic: A boy wheels a bicycle out of the shop and will not let anyone else touch the handlebars: mine, and never anyone's before. mài is new, and it sounds exactly like that my. (▁ low and flat, said with both hands on the bars)
entries.headline: …mài.
entries.scene: A boy gripping the handlebars of a gleaming new bicycle just outside a shop doorway, shoulders hunched protectively, while two other children reach towards it. A shop window full of bicycles behind, hard sunlight on the pavement.

entries.mnemonic: A stallholder sets a heavy jar of orange Tang down on the trestle at dawn and it stands there all day. That is tâng: to set a thing up and leave it standing. Careful — tʰáng with the voice held high is 'all'. (↓ falling, the jar comes down with the voice)
entries.headline: tâng.
entries.scene: Two hands lowering a heavy glass jar of orange powder onto a wooden trestle table at a market, the wood bowing slightly. Other stalls stretch away unopened behind. Early light, empty aisles.

entries.mnemonic: The cake is cut into slices and a sugar swan is set on each one — one swan, one portion, and nobody gets two. sùan is the share: the section, the part of the whole. (▁ low and flat, the knife going straight down)
entries.headline: …sùan.
entries.scene: An overhead view of a large round cake cut into eight even slices on a table, a small white sugar swan standing on each slice, hands reaching in from several sides. A bright party cloth, scattered crumbs.

entries.mnemonic: A rap on the door, and the man opens it to a courier holding out a parcel. He takes it, both hands. Ráp is to receive — a parcel, a guest, a phone call, a job. (▲ high and taut, quick as the knock)
entries.headline: ráp.
entries.scene: A front door half open. A courier on the step holds out a brown parcel; the householder has both hands on it, taking the weight. Van at the kerb behind, rain on the path, grey afternoon.

entries.mnemonic: The parcel comes out of the back of the van and he catches it against his chest without breaking stride. ráp is receiving — taking what comes at you — and it lands with a flat rap. (▲ high and taut, the smack of the catch)
entries.headline: Ráp!
entries.scene: A delivery man on the pavement catching a wrapped parcel against his chest with knees bent, as another man hurls it from the open back of a van. Motion blur on the parcel, stacked boxes in the van, grey morning street.

entries.mnemonic: The first tray out of the oven goes onto the top rack, too hot to touch, while the window is still dark. Stretch it — raaack — and you have rɛ̂ɛk: the first one, the first time. (↓ falling, the tray lands)
entries.headline: rɛ̂ɛk.
