entries.scene: A bakery before dawn. A baker slides a tray of pale rolls onto the top shelf of a tall steel cooling rack, every shelf below it empty. Dark window, flour dust in the lamplight.

entries.mnemonic: A line of orange-robed monks at dawn, bowls out, and the first sound of prayer already in the air. phrá is the monk himself — and the word you put in front of anything holy. (▲ high and taut, one bright syllable)
entries.headline: phrá.
entries.scene: A line of monks in orange robes walking barefoot down a misty street at dawn with alms bowls held at their chests, while a kneeling woman places rice into the first bowl. Soft grey light, shuttered shopfronts, bare feet on wet ground.

entries.mnemonic: A hall of empty chairs and abandoned music stands, and only the piano still playing — only that, nothing else. Take the pian from piano and hum the end in your nose: phiiang, only. (— flat and level, one instrument holding one note)
entries.headline: phiiang…
entries.scene: A vast concert hall with rows of empty chairs and abandoned music stands in darkness, one grand piano lit by a single overhead lamp with a pianist still playing. Dust drifting in the beam of light.

entries.mnemonic: Two people stand in front of a canvas of splashes with their heads tilted. It might be art. It might not. Àat is exactly that hedge — may, might, possibly — said like 'art' with the R swallowed. (▁ low and flat, no commitment in the voice)
entries.headline: àat.
entries.scene: A white gallery wall with one enormous splattered canvas. Two visitors stand well back with their heads tilted at the same angle, one with a hand on his chin. Spotlights, polished concrete floor.

entries.mnemonic: The shopkeeper asks what size and the customer holds up a gnat between finger and thumb: that big. kha-nàat is size — from a gnat to an elephant, it is the same word. (▁ the second syllable drops low and flat, the fingers pinching shut)
entries.headline: kha-nàat.
entries.scene: A shopkeeper leaning over a counter squinting at a customer's raised hand, finger and thumb pinched almost shut on something too small to see, while the shelves behind hold enormous rolled mats beside tiny jars. Warm shop light.

entries.mnemonic: Ask for a different room and the clerk turns to the board of hanging keys for another one. Say 'oon' with the lips spread flat, not pushed forward, and you have ɯ̀ɯn: the other one, some other, a different one from this. (▁ low and flat, a plain alternative)
entries.headline: ʔɯ̀ɯn.
entries.scene: A small hotel desk. A clerk reaches up to a board of keys hanging on hooks, one hand on a key, while a guest waits with a bag at her feet.

entries.mnemonic: A boy picks up a violin he has never touched and plays it perfectly first time. The old teacher points at him and names him on the spot: nák — the one with the knack, the person of that trade. (▲ high and taut, one bright word)
entries.headline: nák…
entries.scene: An elderly music teacher in a cluttered practice room pointing at a small boy who is holding a violin under his chin mid-bow, eyes closed. The other pupils have stopped playing and turned to stare.

entries.mnemonic: First morning of a new term: the bell goes, the gates swing open and a hundred children pour through at once. Rɤ̂ɤm rhymes with term, and a term is the thing that starts. (↓ falling, the bell drops into the yard)
entries.headline: rɤ̂ɤm!
entries.scene: School gates swinging inward with a crowd of uniformed children surging through into a yard, bags swinging, a teacher standing to one side. Long shadows, low morning sun, dust in the air.

entries.mnemonic: The whole crew is out bringing in the crop — grandmother, parents, children, all bent over the same rows. A family is a crop-crew: khrɔ̂ɔp-khruua. (↓ the first half drops hard, the load coming down)
entries.headline: khrɔ̂ɔp-khruua.
entries.scene: Three generations of one family harvesting a rice paddy together at dusk: an old woman bent over the stalks, two adults carrying bundled sheaves on a shoulder pole, two children dragging a basket. Flooded field reflecting an orange sky.

entries.mnemonic: A small boy has claimed the rail at the stern of the ferry and is shouting at the wake. The deck is his. Dèk is a child — short, blunt and low, like the boards under his feet. (▁ low and flat, a short stamp of a word)
entries.headline: dèk.
entries.scene: The stern deck of a wooden ferry. A small boy grips the rail and leans out over the churning white wake, mouth open, hair flat in the wind. Passengers sit behind him in the shade. Bright glare off the water.

entries.mnemonic: The crowd goes rah as the car turns slowly on its stand, and a buyer at the rail holds up a fat brick of banknotes. raa-khaa — a rah and a car — is what the thing costs, and it is the one thing everybody came to hear. (— both syllables flat and level, a price stated plainly)
entries.headline: raa-khaa?
entries.scene: A motor show hall. A gleaming saloon revolves slowly on a turntable under white spotlights while a ring of onlookers cheer with arms raised. At the rail a buyer in a linen suit holds a thick brick of banknotes above his head.

entries.mnemonic: Ask the hundred-year-old woman how she managed it and she taps her temple: cheer, and wit. chii-wít is a life — the whole span of one, in two syllables. (▲ the second syllable snaps up high as her finger taps)
entries.headline: chii-wít.
entries.scene: A very old woman on a wooden porch chair, laughing, tapping her own temple with one crooked finger while three young people crouch around her listening. Cats on the steps, potted plants, soft late afternoon light.

entries.mnemonic: A boy stands rigid against the door frame while his mother lays her hand flat on his head and marks the wood. Taller soon, taller again soon, the marks climbing every year. Sǔung is high, tall, the top end of anything. (↑ rising, like the marks going up the frame)
entries.headline: sǔung!
entries.scene: A kitchen door frame covered in short pencil marks at different heights. A boy stands hard against it on tiptoe while his mother presses one hand flat on his head and reaches with a pencil. Warm hallway light.

entries.mnemonic: A basketball player stands back to back with a small boy and the measuring hand has to climb and climb. Say soon and hum the end into your nose: sǔung, tall. (↑ rising, the voice climbs with the hand)
entries.headline: sǔung.
entries.scene: A very tall basketball player standing back to back with a small boy in a school gym while a teacher on a step stool reaches up with a flat hand to mark the top of the player's head.

entries.mnemonic: He gets to the buffet one minute late and the tray is already gone. He should have come before. Gɔ̀ɔn is before, first, ahead of the other thing. (▁ low and flat, the word lands after the fact)
entries.headline: gɔ̀ɔn.
entries.scene: A function hall after the rush. A man in a suit stares down at an empty steel serving tray with tongs lying across it, crumbs and a smear of sauce left. Stacked chairs, other emptied trays, cold strip lighting.

entries.mnemonic: The bus swings round the bend and every standing passenger leans the same way; at the next stop they all get off and change to another bus. Put a p on lean — plìan — and you have changing, switching, transferring. (▁ low and flat, the lean held steady through the bend)
entries.headline: plìan.
entries.scene: The interior of a crowded bus taking a sharp bend, every standing passenger leaning the same way in unison with hands on the overhead rail. Through the windows another bus waits at a stop ahead. Hot daylight, dust on the glass.

entries.mnemonic: Two cooks taste from the same pot and disagree: one gets a sharp citrus tang, the other gets nothing at all. Different tongues, different tàang. Tàang is different, other, not the same. (▁ low and flat, said with a shrug)
entries.headline: tàang.
entries.scene: Two cooks either side of a steaming stockpot, each with a tasting spoon halfway to their mouth. One is wincing hard, the other shrugging with eyebrows raised. Steel kitchen, steam, overhead lamps.

entries.mnemonic: ต่อ joins on and ไป goes: together they mean carry on to the one after this. The relay runner takes the baton and is gone before the first has stopped — tɔ̀ɔ-pai, next. (▁ the first syllable drops low, the second runs off with him)
entries.headline: tɔ̀ɔ-pai.
entries.scene: A relay handover on a running track: one runner at full stretch pressing a baton into the open backward-reaching hand of the next, who is already accelerating away. Painted lanes, a blurred stadium behind, harsh floodlight.

entries.mnemonic: A hen picks one spot in the whole yard and settles into it; no other spot will do. Say hen and let the end hum in your nose — hɛ̀ng — the place, that particular spot. (▁ low and flat, the hen settling into the dust)
entries.headline: hɛ̀ng.
entries.scene: A single brown hen settled in a shallow dust hollow in the exact middle of an otherwise empty farmyard, feathers fluffed and eyes half shut, while other hens wander round the edges. Hard midday sun, a sharp shadow beneath her.

entries.mnemonic: Every career ladder has the same thing at the top: a chief. aa-chîip is the whole ladder — the trade you follow and where it leads. (↓ falls firmly on the second syllable, the weight of a title)
entries.headline: aa-chîip.
entries.scene: A long ladder rising out of an open-plan office floor and up through a skylight, with workers in different uniforms — cook, nurse, mechanic, engineer — climbing it at different heights. At the very top rung stands a figure in a chief's peaked cap, silhouetted against bright sky.

entries.mnemonic: The lid comes off the basket and the fish inside is longer than the man holding it — yikes. Cut it down to yài and you have big: the fish, the house, the boss. (▁ low and flat, the word lands like the fish on the deck)
entries.headline: yài!
entries.scene: A fisherman on a dock struggling to hold up an enormous fish longer than he is tall, knees buckling, mouth open in astonishment, while a small crowd of onlookers backs away. Bright harbour light, boats and nets behind.

entries.mnemonic: Ràp, to receive, is sitting inside it: sǎm-ràp marks whoever receives the thing. A boy hands over a brown-paper parcel wrapped for a man named Sam — Sam-rap — and it is for him, nobody else. (▁ the second syllable drops low, the parcel changes hands)
entries.headline: sǎm-ràp Sam.
entries.scene: A boy on a doorstep holding out a brown-paper parcel tied with string to a man who has both hands on it. Neither has let go. Terrace houses, milk bottles on the step, flat morning light.

entries.mnemonic: The same phǒm a man uses for himself is the word for the hair on his head: one palm goes to the chest, the other to the crown. The barber lifts the mirror and there it is, what is left of his phǒm. (↑ rising, the voice climbs with the hand)
entries.headline: phǒm.
entries.scene: A barber holding a round hand mirror behind a seated man's head so he can see the back of his fresh haircut, the man patting the top of his own head with one hand.

entries.mnemonic: The bell in the middle of the square is the one that clangs, and every lane in the town runs to it. Klaang is the middle, the centre — and the clang comes from exactly there. (— flat and level, the note held)
entries.headline: klaang.
entries.scene: A high view of a village square with a small open bell tower at its dead centre, four lanes running out from it between tiled roofs. A man swinging the bell rope below. Midday, short shadows.

entries.mnemonic: The grandmother turns the sock over to darn the other side — this side done, that side still holed. dâan is a side, a face, an aspect: whichever one is turned towards you. (↓ falling, the voice drops as the sock is flipped)
entries.headline: dâan.
entries.scene: An old woman by a window turning a woollen sock over a wooden darning mushroom, needle raised in one hand, a basket of mending at her feet. Soft grey daylight, a worn armchair, spectacles low on her nose.

entries.mnemonic: The one who is locked out knocks; the one inside opens. A knock always comes from nɔ̂ɔk — outside, out of, beyond the door. Nɔ̂ɔk is everything past the threshold. (↓ falling, the fist comes down)
entries.headline: nɔ̂ɔk.
entries.scene: A wooden door seen from the wet street, a fist mid-knock against it, rain running off a coat sleeve. Warm light in the window beside the door and a shape moving behind the glass. Night.

entries.mnemonic: One dew drop on the whole leaf, the only one left on the whole bush, and it holds the entire garden upside down inside it. Say dee, then ow, and run them together: diiaw — one, single, the only one there is. (— flat and level, nothing moves at all)
entries.headline: diiaw.
entries.scene: Extreme close view of a single large dew drop hanging from the tip of one green leaf at dawn, the blurred garden behind reflected upside down inside it. The rest of the leaf is dry. Cool blue morning light.

entries.mnemonic: You already say this one: Mɯang Thai, the Thai country — literally the Thai city. A mɯang is a town, and the old kingdoms were single walled towns with their fields around them. Say it 'moo-ang' with the lips spread flat. (— flat and level, both parts even)
entries.headline: mɯang thai
entries.scene: An old walled town seen from a hillside: a moat and brick rampart enclosing tiled temple roofs and lanes, with rice paddies and palms spreading out beyond the wall. Hazy hills on the horizon, warm late light.

entries.mnemonic: Say moo with the lips pulled wide in a grin, then hum the end: mɯang. The town is wherever the cattle market is — one flat bellow carries over the rooftops and everyone knows which town they are in. (— flat and level, one long note held over the roofs)
entries.headline: mɯang.
entries.scene: A hillside view down over a Thai market town at dusk: tiled rooftops, a temple spire, and a cattle pen at the edge where buffalo stand packed together, one with its head raised. Smoke from cooking fires, warm haze.

entries.mnemonic: A busker will sing about anything you drop in his hat — a spanner, an apple, somebody's lost glove. Every one of them is a sìng: a thing, any thing at all. (▁ low and flat, the most ordinary word there is)
entries.headline: sìng.
entries.scene: A street busker with a guitar mid-song, an upturned hat at his feet holding a spanner, an apple and a single glove instead of coins. Two passers-by grinning. Shopfronts, pavement, afternoon light.

entries.mnemonic: At the wedding feast the couple's wrists are bound together with white cord and they feed each other from one torn round of naan. Say TANG NAAN and let the ng of tang run straight on into naan — one bread, one sound, two people joined. (— the second syllable holds level and long, like the vow)
entries.headline: dtàaeng-ngaan.
entries.scene: A bride and groom sit with their wrists bound by a loop of white cord, each lifting a torn piece of flatbread to the other's mouth, both laughing. Guests lean in around the table. Strung lights, petals.

entries.mnemonic: Every head in the barber's chairs has a different cut and every cut has its own song — the quiff hums, the bob swings, the crop marches. Ask for a song and you get a style. soŋ is the shape a thing is styled into. (— flat and level, everyone on the same note)
entries.headline: soŋ.
entries.scene: A barber shop where four customers in a row of chairs all have wildly different hairstyles and are all singing with mouths open, while the barber conducts them with his comb. Mirrors, chrome chairs, bright strip lighting.

entries.mnemonic: The waiter refuses to take a spoken order — everything must be sung. The customer stands, hand on heart, and sings her dinner across the restaurant. You sàng what you sung. (▁ low and flat, even when sung badly)
entries.headline: sàng!
entries.scene: A restaurant dining room. A woman has risen from her table, one hand on her heart and the other flung out theatrically, singing her order toward a waiter who stands to attention with notepad raised, delighted. Other diners turn to watch. Warm chandelier light, white tablecloths.

entries.mnemonic: ใกล้ klâi and ไกล klai are the same handful of sounds and only the tone separates them. The falling one is the one that comes down to you: a bird dropping onto an outstretched hand. The level one keeps going, out to the horizon. Near falls. Far stays flat. (↓ falling, the bird lands on the hand)
entries.headline: klâi.
entries.scene: A woman standing in an open field with one arm held out, a small bird just settling onto her fingers, wings still spread. Far behind her a second bird is a tiny speck against a pale sky above distant hills.

entries.mnemonic: The tattooist stops the needle dead and cuts the line off clean rather than carry it round the arm. tàt is cutting — hair, cloth, price, a line stopped short. (▁ low and flat, the word cut off as sharply as the line)
entries.headline: tàt.
entries.scene: Close view of a tattooist's gloved hands lifting the needle away from a forearm, a bold black line ending abruptly mid-curve on the skin. Ink pots, a wiped paper towel, harsh angled lamp light.

entries.mnemonic: Say poo-an, but grinning — lips pulled wide instead of pushed forward — and you land the Thai vowel exactly: phûuean. Two friends with their arms round each other's shoulders, both grinning like that, are the word and the way to say it in one picture. (↓ falling, warm, the voice settles)
entries.headline: phûuean.
entries.scene: Two young men on a beach at sunset with their arms slung round each other's shoulders, heads tipped together, both grinning enormously with lips pulled wide, sand on their knees, a football at their feet.

entries.mnemonic: The leader of the race comes round the bend alone with the camera bike ahead of him and the pack nowhere in sight. Nam is 'num' with the rest of number cut off: to lead, to take the front, to bring others along. (— flat and level, an even pace)
entries.headline: nam.
entries.scene: A lone marathon runner on an empty road coming round a bend, a motorcycle with a camera rig just ahead of him, crowds pressed against barriers on both sides. Wet tarmac, grey morning.

entries.mnemonic: He takes the turning everyone warned him about and walks straight into the pit, mud up to his chest, looking up at the path he should have taken. phìt is wrong — the wrong one, the mistake. (▁ low and flat, the bottom of the pit)
entries.headline: phìt.
entries.scene: A man standing chest-deep in a muddy pit in a jungle path, arms out for balance, looking up at the proper trail curving safely past above him. Broken branches around the pit edge, green shade, damp earth.

entries.mnemonic: The fridge dies in the night and the whole tray of prawns has turned. She holds one up at arm's length, pulls a face and drops it in the bin: see-ya. Sǐa is spoiled, wasted, broken, gone bad. (↑ rising, the voice lifts on the last of it)
entries.headline: sǐa!
entries.scene: A kitchen at night lit only by an open fridge. A woman holds a prawn at arm's length over a bin with her face turned away, a tray of them on the counter beside her. Harsh white fridge light, dark room.

entries.mnemonic: The gatekeeper stands with folded arms and will not open up until John comes — not a minute earlier. tɕon is the until: everything holds still right up to that point. (— flat and level, the wait unchanging)
entries.headline: …tɕon…
entries.scene: A uniformed gatekeeper standing motionless with folded arms inside a locked factory gate at night, the headlights of an approaching car just beginning to light his face. Empty yard behind, rain on the tarmac, one sodium lamp.

entries.mnemonic: The tow truck hooks up one car and no more: that much, and that is all of it. tʰâw is as-much-as and nán is that — put them together and you have only. (▲ the last syllable snaps up high, the hook locking on)
entries.headline: …tʰâw nán.
entries.scene: A tow truck on a night street with a single small car hoisted on its hook while a whole row of other parked cars sits untouched behind it. The driver leans out of the cab holding up one finger.

entries.mnemonic: A bucket chain at a house fire: the pan of water goes from hand to hand, past each person and on to the next. Say pan with the long ah of father — phàan — to pass by, to go through. (▁ low and flat, the steady rhythm of the chain)
entries.headline: phàan.
entries.scene: A line of villagers strung between a well and a burning wooden house at night, passing a metal pan of water hand to hand, faces lit orange. Smoke and sparks rising, buckets scattered on the ground.

entries.mnemonic: Whatever you bought, you bought it in bàat. The English past tense and the Thai currency are the same sound, and the one always follows the other. (▁ low and flat, the sound of a note being laid down)
entries.headline: bàat.
entries.scene: A close overhead view of a market transaction: a hand laying purple and green Thai banknotes down onto a wooden counter, beside a wrapped parcel tied with string that has just been paid for. The vendor's hands rest on the parcel, about to push it across. Warm stall lighting.

entries.mnemonic: The photograph is torn in two and each half holds a different part of the day: the morning in one hand, the evening in the other. tɔɔn is the stretch of time you mean — the bit you tore out. (— flat and level, both halves held up the same)
entries.headline: tɔɔn…
entries.scene: Two hands holding up the torn halves of one photograph side by side, one half showing a sunlit breakfast table and the other the same table by lamplight. Plain dark background, the torn edge ragged between them.

entries.mnemonic: Set it down, and from that moment on: tâng, to set up, plus tɛ̀ɛ. The jar was stood on the trestle at dawn and has not moved since. Tâng-tɛ̀ɛ marks the point something started and kept going from. (▁ the second syllable drops low, the line running on from there)
entries.headline: tâng-tɛ̀ɛ
entries.scene: A market at dusk, stalls packed away, one bare wooden trestle left with a single heavy glass jar standing on it exactly where it was put. Empty aisle, litter, long orange shadows.

entries.mnemonic: Something under the floorboards reeks and the whole family stands in the doorway calling for the landlord, over and over. rîiak is to call — to call out, to call someone, to call a thing by its name. (↓ falling, each shout drops away at the end)
entries.headline: Rîiak!
entries.scene: A family clustered in an open doorway holding their noses with one hand and waving with the other, shouting up the street, lifted floorboards behind them in a dim hallway. Evening light, a cat fleeing past their feet.

entries.mnemonic: The spoon comes toward the child and he opens his mouth — not to swallow, but to let out one long flat yaaa that goes on until his breath runs out. The syrup goes in anyway. Every dose starts with that noise, and that noise is the word. (— flat and level, held as long as his lungs allow)
entries.headline: yaaa…
entries.scene: A small child on a sofa howls with head tipped back and mouth wide open, fists clenched, as a parent leans in with a spoonful of dark red syrup and a small brown bottle. Lamp-lit living room.

entries.mnemonic: Slip a vowel into the middle of 'smart' and you have sǎa-mâat — and smart is exactly what it means: able to do the thing. A woman crouches at a dead fuse box and brings the stall back to life with a hairpin. (↓ falls on the second syllable, the job done)
entries.headline: sǎa-mâat.
entries.scene: A night market stall gone dark while the ones either side blaze. A woman crouches at an open fuse box with a hairpin between her fingers, the vendor holding a torch over her shoulder. Cables, crates, curious faces.

entries.mnemonic: Say the first syllable of plaza and stop there: plah. A silver fish the length of a man has come up out of the fountain in the town plaza and is flapping about on the flagstones while the whole square backs away from it. plaa is the fish. (— flat and level, said plainly)
entries.headline: plaa!
entries.scene: A paved town square at midday with an ornate fountain at its centre. An enormous silver fish lies flapping on the wet flagstones beside it, water spreading around it, spray still falling.

entries.mnemonic: A fat carp works its mouth against the glass — blah, blah, blah — silent, endless, never changing pitch. bplaa is fish, and the fish stands there saying its own name at you all afternoon. (— flat and level, one long unchanging blah)
entries.headline: blah, blah.
entries.scene: Close on a fat orange carp pressed against aquarium glass, mouth wide open mid-gulp, one round eye staring out. On the other side of the glass a bored child rests her chin on the rim, watching it. Green-lit water, rising bubbles.

entries.mnemonic: One photograph of papa on the wall, and it is the only picture anybody has of him. Say papa and stop halfway — phâap — a picture, an image, the thing that keeps a face. (↓ falling, the voice drops the way a hand lowers a frame)
entries.headline: phâap.
entries.scene: A single framed portrait of an old man hanging alone on a bare wooden wall, with a small shelf beneath it holding incense and a marigold garland. Dust turning in a shaft of light from a high window.

entries.mnemonic: Outside plus from: nɔ̂ɔk, the knock at the door, and jàak, Jack with his suitcase. Everyone came except Jack, who never got past the step — apart from him, the party was complete. (▁ the last syllable settles low, the door stays shut)
entries.headline: nɔ̂ɔk-jàak Jack
entries.scene: A lit front room full of people seen through a window from the dark street, and one man standing outside on the path with a suitcase, looking in. Rain on the glass, his breath fogging, streetlight behind him.

entries.mnemonic: An aunt reads to the whole room without once looking up, one finger moving down the page, and nobody dares interrupt. Say aunt and drop the t: àan, to read. (▁ low and flat, a quiet voice that never lifts)
entries.headline: àan.
entries.scene: An elderly aunt in an armchair reading aloud from an open book on her lap, one finger tracing down the page, four children sitting cross-legged on the floor around her, rapt. Lamplight, drawn curtains, evening.

entries.mnemonic: A glider slips its tow rope and simply keeps going — over the ridge, over the river, until it is a speck a watcher has to squint at. Say GLIDE and drop the d: glai. Whatever it is, it is a long way off. (— flat and level, the word carries without any effort at all)
entries.headline: glai.
entries.scene: A white sailplane hangs far out over a vast green valley, tiny against an enormous sky, its tow rope falling away beneath it. On a ridge a figure shades their eyes, watching. Late afternoon light.

entries.mnemonic: A bowl of green curry lands in front of you and the cook asks whether you have ever had it. Say 'curry' with the R swallowed — kʰɤɤy — and that is the word: ever, have done before, used to. (— flat and level, an even question)
entries.headline: kʰɤɤy?
entries.scene: A bowl of green curry being set down in front of a diner by a smiling cook, steam lifting off it, rice and a spoon beside. Other diners at the long table lean in. Warm lamplight, worn wooden table.

entries.mnemonic: The teacher claps once and every child turns round and comes straight back from the far end of the field. klàp is going back — back home, back the way you came. (▁ low and flat, one clap, no echo)
entries.headline: klàp!
entries.scene: A teacher at the edge of a school field with hands just brought together in a clap, while thirty children scattered across the grass all turn at once and begin running back towards her. Dust, long shadows, late afternoon.

entries.mnemonic: The bride has lost hers somewhere in a reception of two hundred guests, so she calls across the room. One man stands up in the middle of the tables, hand high, thumb jabbing at his own chest: saa, ME. A long open aah, then ME. That is the husband. (↑ sǎa climbs as the hand goes up, then mii sits flat)
entries.headline: saa— ME.
entries.scene: A crowded wedding reception. A bride in white stands on a chair scanning the room, and among the seated guests one man in a dinner jacket has risen, one hand high, the other thumb pointed at his own chest, grinning.

entries.mnemonic: A crow on the café railing caws at every table in turn until somebody gives up a chip. Kʰɔ̌ɔ is asking for — a favour, a discount, one more minute — and the voice climbs the way the caw does. (↑ rising, the call lifts at the end)
entries.headline: kʰɔ̌ɔ…
entries.scene: A seaside café terrace. A crow perched on the railing leans toward a table of chips with its beak open, wings half lifted, while two diners shield their plates with their forearms. Bright overcast light, gulls beyond.

entries.mnemonic: A globe spins on a low table and the boy stops it dead with one finger. Say low and put a k on the end — lôok — the world, the whole of it under one fingertip. (↓ falling, the spin slowing and stopping)
entries.headline: lôok.
entries.scene: A boy leaning over a large old spinning globe on a low table in a dim study, stopping it with one extended finger, his face lit by a desk lamp. Crowded shelves and a brass telescope in the shadows behind him.

entries.mnemonic: The germ of an idea is the first version of it, before anybody improved it. Dɤɤm rhymes with germ and means exactly that: the original, the former, the way it was to start with. A gardener holds up the seed the whole orchard came from. (— flat and level, nothing has moved)
entries.headline: dɤɤm.
entries.scene: An old gardener's open palm holding one wrinkled seed, held out toward the viewer, with rows of heavy fruit trees receding behind him. Soil under his nails, morning light through the branches.

entries.mnemonic: ráp is the catch; dâi in front of it says it actually landed. The parcel smacks into his palm and stays there — dâi-ráp, received, got. (▲ the second word snaps up high with the smack)
entries.headline: dâi-ráp.
entries.scene: A man on a doorstep with a parcel just landing hard in his open palm, his fingers closing round it, a courier already turning away down the path. Motion blur on the courier, a wet garden path, grey morning.

entries.mnemonic: It comes in pairs: yîng this, yîng that — the more it rains, the more the lane floods. Rhyme it with king. One yîng sets the other going and both keep climbing. (↓ falling, though the meaning only goes up)
entries.headline: yîng… yîng…
entries.scene: A flooded narrow lane in heavy monsoon rain, a motorbike pushing a bow wave with water halfway up its wheels, the rider's feet lifted clear. Shophouses either side, rain bouncing off the surface.

entries.mnemonic: Two lines of men lean back on the same rope, one line each side of the mud, and fie on the other lot. Each fàai is a side — and there are only ever two worth naming. (▁ low and flat, the strain held steady)
entries.headline: fàai.
entries.scene: A tug of war across a muddy ditch at a village fair: two lines of men leaning far back on one rope, heels dug in, faces straining, a crowd shouting on both banks. Churned mud, bright overcast light.

entries.mnemonic: The toddler's first word finally comes and the whole room stops dead. Kham sounds like 'come' and means word: one word, the unit you count them in. (— flat and level, a small even sound)
entries.headline: kham.
entries.scene: A living room. A toddler stands holding the edge of a chair with her mouth open mid-sound, and four adults around the room have frozen mid-movement, all turned toward her. Tea going cold, afternoon light.

entries.mnemonic: Two people come round the same corner at the same instant and pop — face to face, nose to nose, both stopped dead. phóp is meeting, and it is over in one syllable. (▲ high and taut, gone in an instant)
entries.headline: Phóp!
entries.scene: Two people colliding face to face at a blind corner of a narrow alley, both rocking back on their heels with arms flung up, dropped shopping bursting on the ground between them. Washing overhead, hard midday light.

entries.mnemonic: Two old friends come round the same corner and nearly collide — pop, there he is, after fifteen years. Phóp is meeting someone, usually the kind of meeting you did not plan. (▲ high, the surprise snaps the voice up)
entries.headline: phóp!
entries.scene: Two men colliding at a busy street corner, bags dropped and spilling, both thrown back a step with their arms up and faces open in recognition. Pedestrians parting around them. Bright pavement, shopfronts.

entries.mnemonic: เข้า is to enter and ใจ is the heart. An idea you understand is one that got through the door and sat down inside you. khâo-tɕai — in it went. (↓ the first syllable drops hard, the door swinging shut behind it)
entries.headline: khâo-tɕai.
entries.scene: A cutaway of a small wooden house with a warm glowing interior, a figure stepping over the threshold out of the dark into the light and shaking rain from a coat.

entries.mnemonic: The English article does the same job: an apple, an egg — one of a thing. ʔan is the all-purpose counter for small objects that have no classifier of their own. Point and say an, and the number of them follows. (— flat and level, a small unstressed word)
entries.headline: ʔan nɯ̀ng
entries.scene: A hardware stall counter with a shallow tray of identical small brass hinges. A customer's finger rests on exactly one of them; the stallholder's hand hovers ready to pick it out. Close crop, oily wood, warm bulb above.

entries.mnemonic: She seals her song inside the envelope and pushes it through the slot of the competition box. sòng is sending: a letter, a parcel, a child off to school. (▁ low and flat, the envelope dropping out of sight)
entries.headline: sòng.
entries.scene: A woman's hand pushing a sealed envelope through the slot of a large wooden competition box in a hotel lobby, a queue behind her holding envelopes of their own. Polished floor, potted palms, bright lobby light.

entries.mnemonic: Point at anything in the lane — the dog, the parked scooter, the pipe dripping on the step — and Thai calls it the same thing: man, said just like the English 'man'. It is 'it', and it does for animals and objects alike. (— flat and level, nothing special about it)
entries.headline: man.
entries.scene: A narrow lane with a sleeping dog, a leaning scooter and a dripping pipe all in frame, and a woman in the foreground gesturing loosely at the whole lot with one open hand. Washing overhead, hot flat light.

entries.mnemonic: Take a nun, add a g, and sit her down: nâng. In Thai you do not ride a bus, you sit it — nâng rót — so the word for sitting is also the word for riding. She drops onto the bench and the truck pulls away. (↓ falling, the weight of someone landing on a wooden bench)
entries.headline: nâng.
entries.scene: The open back of a red songthaew truck bumping along a country road, a nun in a white habit seated on the wooden bench among baskets of vegetables, one hand gripping the rail, her veil lifting in the wind.

entries.mnemonic: She carries the whole tower of baskets up the steps on one upturned hand and never touches the rail. Say too with the lips pulled wide in a grin — thɯ̌ɯ — to hold, to carry, to keep hold of. (↑ rising, the voice climbs with the load)
entries.headline: thɯ̌ɯ.
entries.scene: A woman climbing temple steps balancing a stack of six woven baskets on one upturned palm above her shoulder, the other arm out for balance, chin level. A stone naga balustrade, green trees, bright morning light.

entries.mnemonic: The mother word with the voice pushed up instead of dropped: mɛ̂ɛ is mother, mɛ́ɛ is even — even so, even though. A woman walks the whole way home in the rain even though the bus has passed her twice. (▲ high and taut, held up against the weather)
entries.headline: mɛ́ɛ…
entries.scene: A woman walking along a wet road under a small bent umbrella as a lit bus sweeps past her throwing spray, its windows full of dry passengers. Headlights, puddles, night.

entries.mnemonic: Soon, says the engineer, and the count runs down to nothing. sǔun is zero, and his fingers make the empty circle at the very moment the rocket goes. Soon arrives, the count empties out, and that emptiness is the word. (↑ rising, the voice climbs as the count runs out)
entries.headline: Sǔun.
entries.scene: A dim mission control room at night. An engineer leans back from a glowing console, one hand raised making a circle with thumb and forefinger, eyes on the wide window where a rocket lifts off its pad in a bloom of white exhaust.

entries.mnemonic: A lifter at the bar takes one long breath — the lung fills and the power comes. Kam-lang is power, and it is also the word that puts a verb in the middle of happening: he is lifting, right now. (— both syllables flat, the effort held even)
entries.headline: kam-lang.
entries.scene: A weightlifter mid-lift in a bare gym, chest expanded, bar bending across his shoulders, chalk dust hanging in the light. Plates stacked against the wall, nobody else in the room.

entries.mnemonic: The pan handle comes away in his hand and the whole dinner goes across the floor — pan-hǎa. The ha on the end climbs like a question nobody can answer. (↑ the second syllable climbs, both hands thrown up)
entries.headline: pan-hǎa!
entries.scene: A cook in a home kitchen holding a detached pan handle in one hand and staring down at an upturned pan and a curry spreading across the tiles, a cat already approaching the edge of the mess. Hard overhead light.

entries.mnemonic: The farmer lifts the wooden yoke off the buffalo's neck at the end of the day and the animal's head comes straight up. Yók is to lift, to raise — a glass, a hand, a price, a load. (▲ high, the voice comes up with the yoke)
entries.headline: yók.
entries.scene: A farmer lifting a heavy carved wooden yoke clear of a water buffalo's shoulders at dusk, the buffalo's head rising as the weight goes. Flooded paddy behind, orange sky, mud to the knee.

entries.mnemonic: The opening note is the tone everything after it is tuned to, and a tree's trunk is where every branch starts. Tôn is that beginning — the start of the month, the stem of the plant, the first of a run. (↓ falling, the first note drops into the hall)
entries.headline: tôn.
entries.scene: A conductor's baton at the very top of its lift, the whole orchestra poised with bows raised and lips at mouthpieces, nobody yet playing. Dark hall beyond the stage lights.

entries.mnemonic: The moon in the sky and the moon in the paddy water — the same thing twice over. Say moon with the lips pulled wide instead of pushed forward: mɯ̌an, like, the same as. (↑ rising, the voice climbs from the water to the sky)
entries.headline: mɯ̌an.
entries.scene: A flooded rice paddy at night, perfectly still, with the full moon overhead and its identical reflection in the water, a lone farmer silhouetted between them on a narrow bund. Deep blue night, faint mist.

entries.mnemonic: The tow truck word on its own. Two cars hang off the same beam, one exactly as heavy as the other, and the beam sits level. Tʰâw is equal to, as much as — and it is how you say 'times' in a sum. (↓ falls hard, the hook taking the weight)
entries.headline: tʰâw.
entries.scene: A breakdown truck on a forecourt with a balance beam rigged from its crane, an identical small car hanging from each end, the beam perfectly level. Mechanics standing back with arms folded. Hard daylight.

entries.mnemonic: Three syllables that end in a yam: phá-yaa-yaam. A boy hauls at a yam half out of baked ground, heels dug in and both hands on the leaves, and it will not come. Trying is the whole of the word. (— the last syllable levels out and runs on, like the effort)
entries.headline: phá-yaa-yaam!
entries.scene: A boy in a dry field leaning back at a steep angle with both hands gripping the leafy top of a half-exposed yam, heels dug into cracked soil. A basket waits empty beside him. Hard white sun.

entries.mnemonic: The trader drops the coin on the stone and listens: real gold rings — jing. The fake one beside it only thuds. tɕing is true, real, genuine, and it is the sound the real one makes. (— flat and level, one clear note)
entries.headline: tɕing!
entries.scene: A market trader dropping a gold coin onto a stone slab at his stall, head tilted to listen with one eye closed, a second coin lying flat and dull beside it. Brass scales, cloth pouches, close crop, warm low light.

entries.mnemonic: Before anything stood here somebody sang it up: the foreman hums the shape of the roof and the frame goes up around him. Sâang is to build, to create, to make a thing exist. Stretch it — saaang. (↓ falling, the frame comes down onto its posts)
entries.headline: sâang.
entries.scene: Three builders hauling a timber house frame upright with ropes, one of them mid-song with his head back, sawdust hanging in the light. Half-laid floorboards, tools scattered, bright morning.

entries.mnemonic: Everyone squeezes into the one room for the photograph, and the last two run in and drop to the floor at the front. rûam is joining in, taking part, all of it together. (↓ falling, the voice drops as they settle)
entries.headline: rûam.
entries.scene: Twenty people crammed into a small living room for a group photograph, the front row kneeling, two latecomers sliding in at the edges, everyone laughing. A cat on the back of the sofa. Warm lamplight, flash catching faces.

entries.mnemonic: The night coach runs the whole lot of the way without stopping once — all night, no gap. Tà-lɔ̀ɔt is throughout: all night, all year, always, the stretch with nothing broken in it. (▁ both syllables low and flat, unbroken)
entries.headline: tà-lɔ̀ɔt.
entries.scene: A night coach seen from behind on an empty straight highway, tail lights receding, the road running dead ahead to a vanishing point under a sky full of stars. Dark fields either side.

entries.mnemonic: The butcher lifts a long chain of sausages across the stall and names them down the line, one example after another. tɕʰên is for-example: this one, and this one, and this. (↓ falling, the voice drops at each link)
entries.headline: tɕʰên…
entries.scene: A butcher holding up a long linked chain of sausages at arm's length across his stall, pointing at each link in turn with his other hand while a customer follows his finger. Hooks, a marble counter, cold bright market light.

entries.mnemonic: Nǎng is hide — leather — and a book is what people wrote on before paper. Say 'sue' after it with the lips spread flat and you have nǎng-sǔɯ: a book, and by extension anything written down. (↑ both syllables climb, pages lifting)
entries.headline: nǎng-sǔɯ.
entries.scene: A thick leather-bound volume lying closed on a worn wooden table beside a rolled sheet of untanned hide and a bone stylus. One candle, deep shadow, grain visible in the leather.

entries.mnemonic: À la carte: no set menu, nothing bundled, every single dish standing on its own board at its own price. The waiter holds up three fingers for three dishes and charges for each. lá is exactly that — so much each, one price per item. (▲ high and taut, snapped out straight after the number)
entries.headline: …lá.
entries.scene: A waiter setting down three separate small dishes on a restaurant table, each on its own little wooden board and spaced well apart, while the diner holds up three fingers. White cloth, brass cutlery, warm evening light.

entries.mnemonic: The word kept for a judge, a monk or a minister — closer to 'sir' than to 'you'. It sounds like the 'than' in thank you, and thanking is about the right register: the clerk bows before every sentence. (↓ falling, the head dips with the voice)
entries.headline: thâan.
entries.scene: A panelled antechamber. A young clerk bows from the waist as he holds out a closed file with both hands to a robed elder who is reaching for it. Dark wood, brass lamp, one high window.

entries.mnemonic: A cat on a windowsill lifts its nose, reads the air and knows the rain is coming an hour before you do. aa-kàat is both the air and what it is doing — weather. (▁ the second syllable settles low, like the cat)
entries.headline: aa-kàat.
entries.scene: A cat sitting upright on an open wooden windowsill, nose lifted and eyes half closed, whiskers catching the wind. Beyond the window a dark bank of monsoon cloud is rolling in over rooftops while the street below is still in sunshine. Curtains lifting in the draught.

entries.mnemonic: Not plus say: mâi, the flat refusal, and wâa, war with the R swallowed. No matter what anybody says — war, rain or ruin — the ferry leaves at six. (↓ both syllables drop, the decision already made)
entries.headline: mâi wâa…
entries.scene: A small wooden ferry pulling away from a jetty in heavy rain, the pilot facing forward, while three people on the jetty shout and wave after it with bags at their feet. Grey water, low cloud.

entries.mnemonic: Everything she has ever kept is in that cupboard: string, buttons, the good tin. Say kept and drop the t — kèp — to put away and keep. (▁ low and flat, the door pushed quietly shut)
entries.headline: kèp.
entries.scene: An old woman easing a crowded cupboard door shut with both hands, the shelves inside packed with tins, jars, folded cloth and coiled string. A dim kitchen, one window, soft grey daylight.

entries.mnemonic: Forty moves come down to one pawn pushed onto the last rank. That single square is the result. Phǒn is the outcome of a thing — and also the fruit a tree produces. (↑ rising, the voice climbs as the piece goes forward)
entries.headline: phǒn.
entries.scene: A chessboard from low down: one lone pawn standing on the far rank, a king lying toppled beside it, two hands resting on the table edge either side. Wood grain, angled lamp light.

entries.mnemonic: A string of firecrackers and only some of them go off — bang, bang, a gap, then one more. bâang is some: a few of them, not the lot. (↓ falling, each bang drops away into the gap)
entries.headline: bâang.
entries.scene: A string of red firecrackers hanging from a doorway, three of them blown apart mid-burst with smoke and scraps flying, the rest still whole on the string. Children with hands over their ears behind. Bright daylight.

entries.mnemonic: A cat strolls along the table edge and calmly nudges a tumbler into the void. CAT — OW! — and the glass is gone. Say those two together and you have kɛ̂ɛo. (↓ falls, the way the glass does)
entries.headline: CAT — OW!
entries.scene: A cat on a dining table extends one paw, pushing a drinking glass off the edge; the glass tumbles in mid-air below, water arcing out. Sunlit wooden dining room, shallow focus.

entries.mnemonic: The old man will not be helped up the step; his daughter hovers behind him with both hands out, caring, not touching. kɛ̀ɛ is old — old enough to refuse the arm. (▁ low and flat, said without any fuss)
entries.headline: kɛ̀ɛ.
entries.scene: A very old man gripping a doorframe to haul himself up a high wooden step, jaw set, while his middle-aged daughter hovers behind with both hands raised and not quite touching him. A village house, bright doorway light.

entries.mnemonic: The pen from เป็น again, this time with clay in front of it. A lump on the wheel climbs into a bowl under the potter's hands while you watch it happen. Klaai-pen is to become — what a thing turns into. (— both syllables flat, the wheel turning evenly)
entries.headline: klaai-pen.
entries.scene: A potter's wheel spinning, two wet hands closing around a lump of grey clay that is rising into the walls of a bowl. Slip running down the wrists, water bucket beside, dim workshop light.

entries.mnemonic: Your lungs sit in your back, and your back is the part that comes after you. lǎng does both jobs: the back of the body, and after — whatever follows behind. (↑ rising, the voice climbs as he twists to look behind him)
entries.headline: lǎng.
entries.scene: A man twisting round to look over his own shoulder at his bare back in a bathroom mirror, one hand reaching behind to a sore spot between his shoulder blades. Steam at the edge of the mirror, tiled wall, harsh ceiling light.

entries.mnemonic: The man at the back of the queue has the longest wait of anybody. Lǎng is behind — the back of a thing, and after in time. Long queue, back of it, both in one word. (↑ rising, the voice climbs as he cranes to see the front)
entries.headline: lǎng.
entries.scene: An enormous queue snaking twice around a government building. The last man in line stands on tiptoe craning to see the distant front, bag on the ground at his feet. Hot sun, concrete, hundreds of shoulders.

entries.mnemonic: The florist turns each stem until not one of them juts out of line, then ties the whole thing off. tɕàt is arranging — putting things where they belong, nothing sticking out. (▁ low and flat, each stem pressed down into place)
entries.headline: tɕàt.
entries.scene: A florist's hands turning and pressing the stems of a large bouquet into alignment on a workbench, a length of twine held ready between her teeth. Cut stems and leaves scattered across the bench, cool shopfront daylight.

entries.mnemonic: Say LUKE with the lips pulled wide instead of pushed forward and you land lɯ̂ak. A sergeant walks the line, stops dead in front of one man and puts a finger on his chest: that one, chosen out of everybody. (↓ falling, the finger comes down on him)
entries.headline: lɯ̂ak!
entries.scene: A line of soldiers at attention on a parade ground, a sergeant halted in front of one and pressing a finger to his chest. The chosen man stares straight ahead. Dust, hard light, long row receding.

entries.mnemonic: Put a t on the front of her and you have thəə — which is what it means. A young woman steps up to the counter and the whole queue turns: her turn. (— flat and level, said without emphasis)
entries.headline: thəə.
entries.scene: A young woman stepping forward to a busy ticket counter as the people queueing behind her all turn to look at once. A bright station concourse, blurred crowd, high arched windows, morning light.

entries.mnemonic: Sunrise, and he crouches in the doorway on ONE KNEE to lace his boots before the light is properly up. Not next week, not tomorrow — this day, the one starting now, wan-níi. One knee on the threshold of it. (▲ the second half snaps up high and taut, sharp as the first light)
entries.headline: wan-níi.
entries.scene: A man crouches on one knee in an open doorway tying a work boot, head lifted toward a low orange sun rising over rooftops. Long shadows reach back into the dim hallway. Cool blue, warm gold.

entries.mnemonic: Something enormous flattened the field in the night and left one huge print in the mud. Nobody saw it. A giant ape, kʰong — probably. Kʰong is the hedge you put in front of a guess. (— flat and level, said with a shrug)
entries.headline: kʰong.
entries.scene: A flattened circle in a field of tall corn at dawn with one vast footprint pressed into the mud at its edge. Two farmers stand at the rim, one scratching his head, the other with hands on hips. Mist, grey light.

entries.mnemonic: ที่ is the place and มา is coming: the thîi-maa of a thing is the place it came from. Follow the stream up past the village, past the trees, to the crack in the rock where it starts. (— the second syllable levels out, the walk over)
entries.headline: thîi-maa.
entries.scene: A hiker crouched at the head of a mountain stream where water seeps from a crack in mossy rock, cupping a handful of it, the stream winding far down the valley behind her. Cool green light, ferns, wet stone.

entries.mnemonic: She does the whole tour on her own — no guide, no group, her own bag up all four hundred steps. Tua is the body, eeng is on its own: tua-eeng, oneself, by yourself, the self that did it. (— both syllables flat, an even climb)
entries.headline: tua-eeng.
entries.scene: A lone woman with a rucksack halfway up a long steep temple staircase flanked by carved serpent balustrades, empty steps above and below her. Morning haze, green trees, gold roof just visible at the top.

entries.mnemonic: The tong from ต้อง with 'karn' after it. Wanting is a mild kind of must: the man in the flooded basement must have the tong, and the woman at the hardware counter tɔ̂ng-kaan a new pair. It is want with a spine in it. (— the second syllable levels out, the demand stated plainly)
entries.headline: tɔ̂ng-kaan.
entries.scene: A hardware shop counter. A woman holds up a pair of tongs snapped clean in half toward the shopkeeper, who is already turning to a wall of new ones. Racked tools floor to ceiling, strip lighting.

entries.mnemonic: ต้อง is must — the giant tong in the flooded basement — and ต้องการ is what you must have. The man in the water is not asking for the tong. He needs it. (↓ falls hard on the first syllable, the water still rising)
entries.headline: tɔ̂ng-gaan.
entries.scene: A man standing chest-deep in the water of a flooding basement holding an enormous pair of iron tongs above his head with both arms, mouth open in a shout. Water pouring from a burst pipe, one swinging bulb.

entries.mnemonic: The magician slaps the table — dang — and whips the cloth away to show what was underneath it all along. Sà-dɛɛng is to show, to display, to perform. (— the second syllable holds flat and level, the reveal)
entries.headline: sa-dɛɛng!
entries.scene: A small stage. A magician sweeps a red cloth up and off a table, a brass birdcage revealed beneath it mid-flourish, the cloth still in the air. Footlights, dark auditorium, a few faces in the front row.

entries.mnemonic: Open the wardrobe and the moths have had the lot — every coat, every jumper, nothing left. tʰáng-mòt is all of it, the whole total, with mòt meaning used up entirely. (▁ the second syllable drops flat, nothing left to say)
entries.headline: tʰáng-mòt.
entries.scene: An open wardrobe of ruined woollen clothes hanging in shreds with holes through every garment, a few moths still fluttering in the dim interior while a woman stands staring with her hands at her sides. A bedroom, grey window light.

entries.mnemonic: Put a hum in front of 'eye' and you have it: ngâai. An old woman threads a needle first go with one eye shut and hands it back to the girl who has been trying for ten minutes. Easy. (↓ falling, the hands drop as she finishes)
entries.headline: ngâai.
entries.scene: Close view of weathered hands holding a needle and thread just as the thread goes through, one eye squeezed shut. A young girl's hands wait open below. Sunlit doorway, sewing basket on a lap.

entries.mnemonic: Rhymes with pie, with a J on the front. Thai puts this word inside every feeling: a cool jai is calm, a broken jai is heartbreak, a good jai is kind. Jai is the heart and the mind at once, sitting in the middle of the chest. (— flat and level, no movement in it)
entries.headline: jai.
entries.scene: A woman standing in a temple courtyard with one hand laid flat over her breastbone and her eyes closed, incense smoke drifting across her. Gold stupa blurred behind, early light.

entries.mnemonic: A bowl of dice on the table and the old gambler tells him to take one — any die, it makes no difference which. dai is any: whichever one you like. (— flat and level, a shrug in the voice)
entries.headline: …dai.
entries.scene: A gaming table where a hand hovers over a wooden bowl heaped with identical white dice, while an old gambler opposite shrugs with both palms turned up. Green baize, stacked chips, a low hanging lamp, smoky air.

entries.mnemonic: Six teenagers packed under one shop awning in the rain, shoulders touching, all in the gloom together. Klùm is a group — the huddle, the bunch, the lot of them. (▁ low and flat, nobody moving)
entries.headline: klùm.
entries.scene: Six teenagers crammed under a narrow shop awning in heavy rain, shoulders pressed together, bags held over heads. Grey street, water sheeting off the awning edge, closed shutters behind them.

entries.mnemonic: A long loaf cut into thick chunks, one chunk for each part of the day. Say chunk and drop the k — chûang — a stretch, a spell, a phase of time. (↓ falling, the knife coming down through the loaf)
entries.headline: chûang.
entries.scene: A wooden board with a long loaf cut into four thick uneven chunks and a knife resting across it, morning light from a window falling on the nearest chunk and leaving the far ones in shadow. Crumbs and flour dust.

entries.mnemonic: The father word with the drop taken out: pʰɔ̂ɔ is dad, pʰɔɔ is enough. His enormous paw goes flat over the top of the glass before anyone can pour more. Same paw, level voice. (— flat and level, no drop at all)
entries.headline: phɔɔ.
entries.scene: A dinner table. A big weathered hand lies flat across the mouth of a glass while a bottle tips toward it and stops. Plates pushed back, other hands resting on the cloth. Warm evening light.

entries.mnemonic: The bill comes with everything on it — the drinks, the extra rice, the lot rolled into one number for the whole room. ruuam is gathering it all together: total, included. (— flat and level, one number, no argument)
entries.headline: ruuam.
entries.scene: A large round restaurant table of a dozen diners, one man at the centre holding up a single long curl of paper in both hands while everyone leans in towards it. Cleared plates, empty bottles, a warm overhead lamp.

entries.mnemonic: The doorman looks at one face after another and says nah to each of them. Nâa is the face — and also the front of anything: the front of the queue, the front of a shirt, the week in front of this one. (↓ falling, flat refusal straight to the face)
entries.headline: nâa.
entries.scene: A club doorway at night. A doorman's flat palm rests against the chest of the next man in line while he looks past him at the others. Red lamp above the door, velvet rope, faces in the queue.

entries.mnemonic: A boy so keen to get it down that he starts before he sits, the pen already moving as he drops onto the bench. khǐan is to write, and the keenness is in the rising voice. (↑ rising, the voice climbs like his hand lifting off the page)
entries.headline: khǐan.
entries.scene: A schoolboy dropping onto a bench mid-stride with an open notebook on his knee and a pen already touching the page, his satchel still swinging from one shoulder. A courtyard, other children walking past, bright morning.

entries.mnemonic: A boy at the paint counter prises the lid off one tin after another to see what is actually inside each one, because colour is the thing you can only know by looking. Sǐi is colour, and it sounds exactly like 'see'. (↑ rising, the lid comes up)
entries.headline: sǐi.
entries.scene: A hardware shop paint counter. A boy levers the lid off a tin of bright blue paint with a screwdriver, a row of already-opened tins of different colours beside him, lids stacked. Bright shop light.

entries.mnemonic: Every morning the same man takes the same seat at the same tea stall and puts his coin down without a word: the chai man. tɕhaai is a man — the male one, as against the woman at the next table. (— flat and level, the same note every morning)
entries.headline: tɕhaai.
entries.scene: A weathered man in a short-sleeved shirt sitting alone at the corner table of a small tea stall with a glass of milky tea and a single coin in front of him, staring out at the street. Early light, steam, empty chairs.

entries.mnemonic: A bin lid goes over on the tiles at two in the morning — dang — and the whole street knows about it. Dang is loud, and a person who is dang is famous for exactly the same reason. (— flat and level, the noise hanging on)
entries.headline: dang!
entries.scene: A metal bin lid spinning to a stop on dark courtyard tiles, a cat streaking away from the overturned bin, and two upstairs windows lighting up. Night, wet stone, one bare bulb over a door.

entries.mnemonic: The door swings open for one second and the cat is through it and gone — oh, the cat. ʔoo-kàat is a chance: the gap, and whether you went through it. (▁ the second syllable drops low, the door swinging shut)
entries.headline: ʔoo-kàat!
entries.scene: A cat streaking through the narrowing gap of a front door that is swinging shut, only its tail and hind legs still inside, while a man with shopping bags stands startled in the doorway. Hallway light, a rainy street behind.

entries.mnemonic: Say 'summer' the British way with the R swallowed, and push the end up: sà-mɤ̌ɤ. Summer always comes back, every single year, whether anyone asks for it or not. Sà-mɤ̌ɤ is always. (↑ rising, the last syllable climbs like the heat)
entries.headline: sà-mɤ̌ɤ.
entries.scene: A village pond dried back to cracked mud at its edges, three children paddling in the shallow middle of what is left, a buffalo lying in the shade. Hard white sunlight, dry trees, no cloud.

entries.mnemonic: She lifts a tiny gold ring off the velvet and the jeweller calmly builds the stack of banknotes it will cost beside it, a stack taller than the ring is wide. The pang goes straight through her chest. phaaeng: expensive. (— flat and level, the price is not negotiable)
entries.headline: phaaeng.
entries.scene: A jeweller's counter under bright spotlights. A small gold ring sits on a velvet pad; beside it the jeweller has built a tall stack of banknotes. The customer has one hand pressed flat to her chest, leaning back, eyes wide.

entries.mnemonic: The boss's eye is on the whole floor — one eye, and nobody moves. Put an n in front of eye and you have naai: mister, boss, the one you address properly. (— flat and level, with no warmth in it)
entries.headline: naai.
entries.scene: A supervisor standing on a raised platform at the end of a factory floor, hands behind his back, staring down the rows while every worker keeps their head bent over the bench. Long fluorescent strips, pale green machinery.

entries.mnemonic: Eight in the morning and the whole country stands still for one song. Say 'chart' with the R swallowed and you have châat: the nation — and also a whole lifetime, this one and the next one along. (↓ falling, the flag reaches the top as the voice drops)
entries.headline: châat.
entries.scene: A school yard at morning assembly: rows of children standing rigid facing a flagpole, a flag halfway up, two older pupils at the rope. Long shadows across the concrete, low sun.

entries.mnemonic: The whole class leans in over the one book on the desk, heads almost touching. riian is to learn — and Thais often soften that r towards an l, so leaning in gets you there. (— flat and level, a patient classroom note)
entries.headline: riian.
entries.scene: Six schoolchildren crowded round one small desk, all leaning in over a single open book with their heads nearly touching, one girl pointing at the page. A wooden classroom, ceiling fan, hot bright light through louvred windows.

entries.mnemonic: Rian is lean and learn in one word: the boy at the back is bent so far over his desk that his nose is nearly on the page. Rian is to study, and Thais themselves often say the r as an l. (— flat and level, the long hours)
entries.headline: rian.
entries.scene: A classroom at dusk with every desk empty but one. A boy is bent right down over his desk, nose almost touching it, a small lamp beside him. Chalk dust, shuttered windows, blue light outside.

entries.mnemonic: A cicada in the tree sings so loudly the whole street looks up. Stretch sing into see-ang and you have sǐang: a sound, a voice, a noise. (↑ rising, the voice climbs the way the cicada's does)
entries.headline: sǐang.
entries.scene: A single large cicada clinging to the bark of a street tree with its wings blurred, while three pedestrians below have stopped and tilted their heads up towards it. Hot white daylight, dappled leaf shadow on the pavement.

entries.mnemonic: Dawn in a camp: the cook bangs a ladle on the pot and the whole sleepy line shuffles up for chow. Breakfast is the first thing that happens in a Thai morning, and cháaw is the morning itself. (▲ high and bright, a shout across a cold yard)
entries.headline: Cháaw!
entries.scene: Dawn in a field camp. A cook in an apron ladles steaming rice porridge into the tin bowls of a queue of sleepy workers, their breath showing in the cold.

entries.mnemonic: Roong is the big shed you put a thing inside: roong plus study is a school, roong plus film is a cinema, roong plus sick is the hospital. Say it like 'wrong' with the o drawn out. (— flat and level, a plain roof over everything)
entries.headline: roong.
entries.scene: A long corrugated-iron hall at the edge of a town, doors standing open at both ends so daylight shows straight through, bicycles leaning along its side wall. Dust, palms, hard midday sun.

entries.mnemonic: Cut the bark and the sap tells you whether the tree is alive — the old forester knows by looking. Say sap with the long ah of father: sâap, the polite word for knowing. (↓ falling, the voice drops with the knife)
entries.headline: sâap.
entries.scene: An old forester pressing his thumb against a fresh cut on a tree trunk where pale sap is beading out, nodding slightly, a small knife in his other hand. Deep green forest shade, shafts of light through the leaves.

entries.mnemonic: Say 'chew' with the lips spread flat and let it fall away into 'ah': chɯ̂a. A woman is told the plank bridge will hold and steps onto it anyway. Believing is doing it before you know. (↓ falling, the foot comes down)
entries.headline: chɯ̂a.
entries.scene: A woman putting her weight onto the first plank of a rope-and-board bridge over a misty gorge, one hand gripping the rope, the other out for balance. Boards missing further along. Cold grey light.

entries.mnemonic: At the end of a long day a man hauls himself up the stairs like a ton of bricks — his own self, the heaviest thing he owns. ton is the self. (— flat and level, one step at a time)
entries.headline: ton.
entries.scene: An exhausted man hauling himself up a narrow concrete stairwell by the handrail, one foot on the next step, head down, jacket over his shoulder. A bare bulb, peeling paint, night outside a small window.

entries.mnemonic: The doctor holds the stethoscope to a man's back and keeps circling one finger: more breath, and more, and more. Say MORE the British way, with no r on the end, and you have mǎaw — the one person who always wants another deep breath out of you. (↑ rising, climbing like the eyebrows above the mask)
entries.headline: mǎaw.
entries.scene: A doctor in a white coat presses a stethoscope to the bare back of a seated patient, one finger raised and circling for another breath. The patient's chest is swelled, eyes wide. Bright clinic, cool daylight.

entries.mnemonic: The doctor tips a spoonful of syrup into the boy and, before he has finished swallowing, is already filling the spoon again. More. More rest, more water, more of this. mǎaw is the doctor, and more is what she always wants. (↑ rising, the voice lifts with the spoon)
entries.headline: mǎaw: more.
entries.scene: A small clinic room. A doctor in a white coat with a stethoscope round her neck holds a brimming spoon of dark syrup toward a boy on the examination couch, the bottle in her other hand already tilted to refill it.

entries.mnemonic: The decorator dabs a mark of paint along the wall at exactly the height of his string line, each dab level with the last one. Rá-dàp is the level: the grade, the rank, the height a thing has got to. (▁ the second syllable drops low, the dab lands)
entries.headline: rá-dàp.
entries.scene: A bare room being decorated. A hand dabs paint onto a wall in a row of small marks that follow a taut string line pinned across it. Ladder, dust sheets, open tin on the floor. Flat daylight.

entries.mnemonic: A pert little housemaid throws the shutters back and the whole room fills with light. Say pert without the r and with an unaspirated p — bpə̀ət — to open, to switch on. (▁ low and flat, the shutters banging back)
entries.headline: bpə̀ət.
entries.scene: A young housemaid in an apron flinging a pair of tall wooden shutters wide open in a dark panelled room, morning light flooding across the floorboards with dust hanging in the beam. Her face turned into the light.

entries.mnemonic: Pert, like the shop that opens dead on time with its shutter snapped up in one movement. Bpɤ̀ɤt rhymes with pert and means to open — a door, a shop, a bottle, a switch. (▁ low and flat, the shutter goes up in one go)
entries.headline: bpɤ̀ɤt.
entries.scene: A shopkeeper rolling a metal shutter up above his head in one sweep, the dark shop interior appearing beneath it. Empty street, awning half unfurled, first pale light down the road.

entries.mnemonic: Cut the pie open and it is all in there: the filling, the steam, the whole dinner. phaai-nai is within — inside the crust, inside the hour, inside the building. (— flat and level, the steam rising evenly)
entries.headline: phaai-nai.
entries.scene: A steaming pie cut open on a kitchen table with one wedge lifted away on a slice to show the dark filling inside, steam rising into window light. An oven cloth, a chipped plate, a deep brown crust.

entries.mnemonic: Say 'lure' with the lips spread flat and lift it: lɯ̌a. One prawn is left on the plate and nobody will take it, sitting there as a lure for whoever gives in first. Lɯ̌a is what is left over. (↑ rising, the voice lifts on the last one)
entries.headline: lɯ̌a.
entries.scene: A nearly bare serving plate in the middle of a crowded table with one prawn left on it, four hands hovering nearby without committing. Empty shells, crumpled napkins, beer glasses, warm light.

entries.mnemonic: He came home from the beach with a tan instead of a burn, because somebody else took the chair in the full sun. tʰɛɛn is in place of — this one instead of that one. (— flat and level, said with a shrug)
entries.headline: tʰɛɛn.
entries.scene: Two men side by side on a beach: one golden brown and relaxed in the shade of a palm, the other lobster red and wincing in the open sun. Deck chairs, turquoise sea, hard afternoon light.

entries.mnemonic: A mongoose up on its hind legs, absolutely still, eyes fixed on one point in the grass. Mɔɔng is that: looking at something, holding your eyes on it rather than merely seeing it. (— flat and level, the stare held steady)
entries.headline: mɔɔng.
entries.scene: A mongoose standing upright on a termite mound, head and eyes locked on one spot in dry grass below, body rigid. Low golden light, long shadow, scrub stretching away behind.

entries.mnemonic: Every relative in the province is in the yard: forty of them on plastic chairs, and you are introduced to all forty. Yâat is a relative, said like 'yard' with the R swallowed. (↓ falling, the introductions keep coming)
entries.headline: yâat.
entries.scene: A crowded courtyard of plastic chairs packed with dozens of people of all ages dressed in white under a marquee, a young man being led along a row shaking hands. Hot afternoon, fans, tea urns.

entries.mnemonic: One photograph of the whole group, and it is the only picture of them all together. Take the roup off group — rûup — a picture, an image, a photo. (↓ falling, the voice drops as the shutter closes)
entries.headline: rûup.
entries.scene: An old framed group photograph of a large family standing in rows outside a village house, hanging slightly crooked on a bare wall from a single nail, a vase of flowers on a shelf below. Warm side light, faded paper.

entries.mnemonic: A tit — the small bird — clamps onto the fat ball hanging from the branch and hangs there upside down for an hour, refusing to let go. Tìt is stuck to, attached to, caught on, addicted to. (▁ low and flat, clamped on)
entries.headline: tìt.
entries.scene: A small blue and yellow bird clinging upside down to a hanging fat ball on a bare winter branch, wings tight to its body, claws locked. Frost on the twigs, pale garden behind.

entries.mnemonic: She lowers the Wang handbag onto the table with both hands, squares it up and takes her hands away. She is not putting it down, she is placing it. waang is exactly that: setting a thing down deliberately and leaving it. (— flat and level, the bag settling without a sound)
entries.headline: waang.
entries.scene: A woman's two hands lowering an expensive black leather handbag onto a polished café table and squaring it precisely, her face out of frame. A marble surface, a coffee cup pushed aside, bright window reflections.

entries.mnemonic: Try getting a yak up a hill it does not fancy. It plants four feet and the entire expedition stops where it stands. Yâak is difficult — the long drawn yaaak of an animal that will not move. (↓ falling, the voice drops with the load)
entries.headline: yâak.
entries.scene: A loaded yak standing immovable on a steep stony mountain path, two guides hauling on a rope from above with their heels dug in. Thin cold air, prayer flags, snow peaks behind.

entries.mnemonic: The naan comes out of the oven longer than the table and it takes the whole evening to get through it. naan is a long time — the bread and the waiting are the same word. (— flat and level, the evening going on and on)
entries.headline: naan.
entries.scene: An enormous naan bread stretching the full length of a restaurant table and hanging off both ends, four diners along one side tearing pieces from it while a waiter carries in more. Warm light, a tandoor glowing behind.

entries.mnemonic: An old post room where every canister goes bop into its brass tube and lands in the right room three floors away. Rá-bòp is the system: the works, the way the parts fit together. (▁ the second syllable drops low, the canister lands)
entries.headline: rá-bòp.
entries.scene: A sorting room walled with brass pneumatic tubes, one canister dropping into a wire basket while a clerk in shirtsleeves reaches for it. Other clerks at benches, dusty light from high windows.

entries.mnemonic: phûu is the one-who and yǐng is the yin: the person of the yin side. Her name is called and a woman rises out of the seated crowd. (↑ the second syllable climbs, the head lifting with it)
entries.headline: phûu-yǐng.
entries.scene: A woman standing up out of a seated crowd at a village ceremony, chin lifting, hands pressed together in front of her, everyone else still seated and turned towards her. Folding chairs, marigold garlands, bright outdoor shade.

entries.mnemonic: Nah — the tea is not ready, it wants another minute. naa-thii is that gap exactly: the sand running through while the leaves open and nobody does anything useful. Nah, tea. Sixty seconds and not a second less. (— both syllables flat, the way a minute just sits there)
entries.headline: naa-thii.
entries.scene: A kitchen counter in morning light. A squat teapot steams beside a small hourglass timer, its sand halfway run through.

entries.mnemonic: Three flat pats and a long last note: phát-thá-naa. A man pats wet concrete smooth over what was a dirt lane, and by evening the lane is a road. Phatthanaa is to develop — the word on every notice about progress. (— the last syllable levels out long and flat)
entries.headline: phát-thá-naa.
entries.scene: A man crouched on a plank laid over fresh wet concrete, patting and smoothing the surface with a float, the unfinished dirt lane still visible ahead of him. Neighbours watching from doorways, late sun.

entries.mnemonic: The whole village sang together at the festival, and afterwards every one of them came to the same long table to eat. sǎng-khom is society: the people who sang and then came — the ones who do both those things together. (— the second syllable levels out, everyone seated at last)
entries.headline: sǎng-khom.
entries.scene: A long communal table under strings of bulbs in a village square, forty people of all ages seated shoulder to shoulder passing dishes along, a few still standing and clapping. Warm night, food steam, dark trees beyond.

entries.mnemonic: English has half of it already: you don't know jack. Rúu is to know and jàk finishes it — rúu-jàk is knowing a person, being acquainted. Two men shake hands at a party and find they grew up on the same lane. (▁ the second syllable drops low, the handshake lands)
entries.headline: rúu-jàk!
entries.scene: Two middle-aged men gripping each other's hand at a crowded party, both leaning back with their free hands on each other's shoulders, mouths open in recognition. Drinks abandoned on a sideboard, warm light.

entries.mnemonic: The driving instructor has given up. Every time the learner drifts the wrong way he tips his head back, lets out a long theatrical sigh and jabs his thumb over his own left shoulder. Sigh, and point left: sáai. (▲ high and taut, the pitch of a man at the end of his patience)
entries.headline: sáai!
entries.scene: A driving instructor in the passenger seat slumps with head tipped back and eyes shut, cheeks puffed in a long exhale, thumb jabbed over his own left shoulder. The learner grips the wheel. Flat grey daylight.

entries.mnemonic: Rows and rows of jam jars on the pantry shelf, and the only question anybody asks is how many: the jam-number. tɕam-nuuan is an amount, a quantity, a count. (— flat and level, counting along the row)
entries.headline: tɕam-nuuan.
entries.scene: A long pantry shelf packed end to end with identical jars of dark red jam, a woman halfway along it with one hand raised, mid-count. Cool larder light from a small high window, a stone floor.

entries.mnemonic: A toddler gets hold of the photographer's lens cap and within a minute it is a spinning top, a wheel and a hat. Lên is to play — with a toy, a sport, an instrument, or anything that was not a toy until now. (↓ falling, the cap lands and spins)
entries.headline: lên.
entries.scene: A toddler sitting on a wooden floor spinning a large black lens cap like a top, an open camera bag beside her and a camera body just out of reach. Afternoon light across the boards.

entries.mnemonic: The lifeboat is going down by the stern, so over the side go the suitcases, the chairs, the oars, everything. What he will not let go of is one dented tin can of water held hard against his chest. Some can. sǎm-khan is the thing that actually matters. (↑ sǎm climbs, then khan lands flat and certain)
entries.headline: sǎm-khan.
entries.scene: An overloaded wooden lifeboat low in a grey swell. A man at the stern heaves a suitcase over the side with one arm while the other clamps a dented tin can tight against his chest. Other passengers cling to the gunwales, soaked.

entries.mnemonic: An electrician holds his meter up to a bare bulb to see how many watts it is pulling, and the needle swings across and settles. wát is that act — measuring, finding out how much of a thing there actually is. (▲ high and tight, the needle flicking up the dial)
entries.headline: wát.
entries.scene: A dim workshop. An electrician on a wooden stepladder holds a handheld meter up toward a bare bulb hanging on a cable, its needle mid-swing across a round dial, his face lit warm from below by the filament.

entries.mnemonic: A traveller points up at a gold-spired roof over a courtyard wall and turns up his palm: what is that? The old guide beside him only nods once and says wát. Question and answer are the same sound, and the answer is always a temple. (▲ high and taut, cut off short by the last consonant)
entries.headline: Wát.
entries.scene: A traveller with a camera points up at a gold-spired temple roof, mouth open, his other palm turned up in a shrug, while an elderly guide beside him nods, hands clasped. Courtyard wall, hot white sky.
